The heading gear was the only way into a connection's settings, and there are two views with no
heading: the name sort flattens every group into one unlabelled list, and a connection whose
every model is pinned has no group left at all. A row with no heading over it now carries a
Connection settings entry in its menu. Rows under a heading still do not, since that would offer
the same destination twice, which is why the entry was taken off them in the first place.

* Studio: applying a model's pin must not rewrite the chat-wide effort

setReasoningEffort goes through setScalarSettingVersion, which persists the value with
saveSettingsPatch as the global reasoning effort (or captures it as the open chat's). So pinning
a connected model to high also moved the chat-wide preference every other model inherits, and
clearing the pin persisted the resolver's provider default in its place. A per-model setting was
overwriting the setting it exists to override.

The dialog now applies the resolved level with a plain setState, which is what the model switch
and both normalization effects already do; the pin itself is still stored by
setModelReasoningEffort. The dialog was the only writer using the persisting action.

* Studio: remember the level a reasoning pin displaced, and advance the settings epoch

Clearing a pin resolved from the live level, which IS the pin: the pin is applied straight to
reasoningEffort, so for a ladder with no catalogue default, no "medium", and a provider that is
neither OpenAI nor Anthropic the resolver falls through to clamping current and handed the pin
straight back. 69 catalogue entries have such a ladder, DeepSeek's low/high/max among them.

Nothing recorded what the pin took the place of. A pin writes the live store with a plain
setState and persists nothing, and the thread snapshot is read off that same live store, so
neither the thread's own value nor the installation default is pin-free. The chat store now keeps
that one level: noted before a pin overwrites the live effort, first displacement winning so
pinning twice and clearing returns to the chat's own level, taken when a pin is cleared, and
dropped when the user states a level themselves through setReasoningEffort. Session only, since
after a reload the live level already is the pin's and nothing preceded it.

Both live writes also advance queuedSettingsEpoch again, which setReasoningEffort used to do for
them. A prompt waiting on startup captures that epoch and rejects itself when it moves, so
without the bump one could dispatch with the effort it captured before the change, and the
queue's own restore of the captured settings would put the old level back.

* Wait for hydration before recording the effort a pin displaced

The normalization effect also runs before chat settings hydrate, when the live
reasoning effort is still the store's own "medium" default rather than the
level the user had persisted. With a pin already set for the restored
checkpoint, that pass recorded "medium" as the displaced level, and because the
record keeps its first value, the rerun after hydration could not replace it.
Clearing the pin later in the session then dropped the chat back to "medium"
instead of the persisted level.

Guard the record in the store, so all four pin sites get it: a pin advances no
mutation version, so hydration replaces the live level with the server's, and
the effect reruns once it lands with the chat's real level in hand.

* Keep a per-model effort pin out of the chat's own settings

reasoningEffort is a thread-scoped setting, so every snapshot taken while a
model pin was in force stored the model's level as the chat's own: any later
thread edit rewrote the row from the live store, and clearing the pin could not
undo it because the snapshot was never revisited. The same live read seeds the
defaults every chat without a snapshot follows.

Hold the pin back at all three points, the way the snapshot already holds back
a permission level and a forced-on thinking toggle: the chat keeps the level it
is on record with, and the pin stays a model-level override. Applying a thread
snapshot now records its level without putting it over the pin, which outranks
the chat for as long as its model is selected, and clearing the pin resolves
from the recorded level first, so it survives a reload and a thread switch.

Also reconcile the pin after a catalogue refresh. A refresh decides which
levels a stored pin is legal against, so it can make a pin that was ignored at
selection time the valid one, and neither the pin effect (its guard sees no
change in the stored string) nor the refresh itself applied it. One shared
reconciler now serves both triggers.

* Hand the chat's own effort back when a pin stops applying

Two places kept running on a pin that no longer applied.

Selecting an unpinned external model resolved the target from the live level,
which is the outgoing model's pin, so with a chat on low, a model pinned to
high and a target offering low/high/max with no published default, the target
inherited high. The displaced level was never consumed because only clearing a
pin read it. Unpinned targets now resolve from it, on the switch and in the
normalization pass, which covers a checkpoint that changes without going
through the switch.

A catalogue refresh that withdraws the level in force was the same story from
the other end: the pin stops counting as a pin, the reconciler returned early,
and the level left in the store was the refresh's clamp of the withdrawn pin,
which the next thread snapshot would then store as the chat's own.

Both read one predicate rather than the stored pin. The record of what a pin
displaced is cleared the moment the user states a level themselves, so it is
the only signal that says the level on screen actually came from a pin.

* Restore the chat's effort before loading a local model, and read the cap in full

Selecting a local model takes its own branch, which never touched the effort:
the load and status handlers clamp whatever the store holds to the local
model's ladder, and what it held was the external model's pin, so a chat set to
low that had a model pinned to high ran the local model at high. Restore the
displaced level at the top of that branch, before the load reads it. A local
checkpoint has no pin of its own, so this only ever puts back what the external
model displaced.

Also parse the whole output cap. A number field accepts scientific notation and
parseInt stops at the "e", so 1e5 was read as 1 and saved clamped to the
provider minimum rather than as 100,000. Number handles the exponent, rejects
junk as NaN, and reads a blank as 0, which the existing positive check already
treats as no value; the result is rounded because the cap is a token count and
the field admits a decimal.

* Let the open chat keep its own prompt when a model's is saved

systemPrompt is one of the chat's own keys, which is why a model switch lays
the chat's values back over the replay. The dialog's live overlay went straight
past that, so saving a model prompt while a chat held its own sent the model's
for the rest of the conversation and the next thread-scoped write would have
stored it as the chat's own. Route the overlay through the same restore, live
params only, so the row still remembers the model's value.

The cap is unaffected: maxTokens is not a chat-owned key, so it lands as
before.

Advance the queued-settings epoch with it, as setParams does. A queued prompt
waiting to start, or a paste still reading its file, compares that epoch
against the one it captured, and without the bump both could go out with the
prompt and cap the dialog had just replaced.

* Keep the pin and the composer's level from disagreeing

Setting a level in the composer while the selected model was pinned left the
pin standing: the level ran now, the row still named the pinned one, and the
next switch or provider resync put it back. Every caller of setReasoningEffort
is the user picking a level for the model on screen, which is what its pin
claims to decide, so the pin goes with the edit. Re-picking the pin's own level
states nothing new and keeps it.

That also removes the reconciler's flag for whether an absent pin means a
cleared one. Whether the level in the store came from a pin is now always asked
of the store, which is the only safe question: a composer edit clears the pin
too, and resolving afresh there would have put the chat's stored level over the
one just chosen.

Pinning the level a chat is already running recorded no displacement, so a pin
in force did not count as owning the live level. Opening a thread with a level
of its own then held that level back behind the pin with nothing to hand back,
and leaving the model ran it at the pin's level. A pin in force now counts on
its own, and the apply records the open chat's level as it holds it back.

* Restore the effort where a local load starts, not where one is picked

Picking an uncached local model does not change the model: stageOrLoad queues
the download and returns, leaving the pinned external model running. Restoring
the chat's effort at the pick therefore ran that model at the chat's level for
the length of the download, and a cancelled or failed download left it there
with no checkpoint change to bring the pin back.

Moved to stageOrLoad, immediately before selectModel, which is past both
staging returns and is the one point every local load funnels through, so it
also covers the deferred load after a staged download completes, which never
went through the pick at all.

* Hand the chat's effort to the clamp, not to the model pick

The pick was still too early. selectModel can return without changing the
model when the lifecycle lease is unavailable, when the user declines the
stop-running-chats confirmation, when a load is already in flight, or when a
Hub token prompt is declined. Each left the pinned external model running at
the chat's level with the record already consumed, and no checkpoint change to
bring the pin back.

Give the level to the two clamps instead, which is where it was always going:
the load response handler and applyActiveModelStatusToStore both narrow the
chat's level to the resident model's ladder, and a pin's level is one model's
rather than the chat's. Both run only once a local model has actually become
resident, so nothing is taken on a path that changes no model, and both are
guarded against running under an external selection, so a pin cannot be
consumed while its own model is still the one selected.

* Copy the model ID through the shared clipboard helper

navigator.clipboard is undefined in the desktop shell and in any insecure
context, such as a Studio reached over plain HTTP on a LAN address, so reading
.writeText off it threw synchronously and the promise's catch never ran: the
menu item did nothing and said nothing. copyToClipboard already handles the
Tauri clipboard, a rejecting Clipboard API and the execCommand fallback, and
reports success as a boolean, which is how every other copy action in Settings
raises its toasts.

* Stop claiming video generation on connected rows

The name heuristic was the only evidence behind that glyph, and a connected row
is selectable: nothing we connect to serves video generation through the chat
route and no provider publishes a capability for it, so the badge and the
Model info line promised something picking the model cannot do. An On Device
row can still say it, where the badge describes a repo you may be about to
fetch rather than a model you are about to chat with.

Nothing is lost by name: detectCapabilities already suppresses imageGen for a
video-named model, so such a row now draws no generation glyph at all, which
is what the app can actually back.

* Only offer an effort where one is sent, and drop the remaining name guesses

The default low/medium/high ladder is present on every external model's
capabilities, including those whose style carries a bare thinking on/off, and
the external request path sends reasoning_effort for the reasoning_effort style
alone. So the row's settings dialog let a level be pinned on Kimi K2.6 that no
request could carry, the info box listed a ladder the model does not take, and
selecting such a model moved the chat's own level through the resolver's
provider default, changing what every other model ran at.

One predicate now answers it, and all three read it: the control is offered
only where a level is sent, the info box lists the ladder and the pin only
there, and the resolver leaves the level alone otherwise.

Image generation loses its name fallback too, for the reason video did. The
adapter enables it through providerSupportsBuiltinImageGeneration alone, and
the composer's Images pill with it, so a name reading like a diffusion model
but resolving to false there could never be asked for an image while the badge
and the "Generates images" filter both said otherwise. Audio keeps the
catalogue's published input modality and nothing else, leaving no mark on a
connected row resting on a guess.

* Check the effort draft against the ladder it will be saved against

The dialog subscribes to the live catalogue, so a refresh while it is open
recomputes which levels the model offers, but a level already picked sat in
state and was saved as-is. Every resolver then refused the pin, since
pinnedReasoningEffort drops a level the ladder does not list, leaving a stored
setting that did nothing.

The draft is now read against the current ladder: one the model no longer
offers reverts to what is stored, and Save treats the field as untouched rather
than writing a pin that cannot apply. A stored pin the ladder has dropped reads
as Follow chat, in the dialog and in Model info, which is what it now does.

* Fix reasoning preference persistence and pin restoration

Store effort pins independently so cross-tab edits cannot overwrite other models.
Keep explicit thread and global effort preferences separate from live model pins.
Restore the chat preference when clearing a pin without changing selection defaults.
Share pin reconciliation and add behavioral regression coverage.

* Apply a connected-pin toggle to the stored list

A write replaces the whole list, and the toggle derived the new one from this
window's copy, so two windows pinning different connected models before the
storage event landed kept only the second pin. The change now goes onto the
stored list, the way the effort pins are now stored per model for the same
reason.

Read as null rather than empty when there is nothing there, distinguishing an
unwritten key or unavailable storage from an empty list: falling back to []
would drop the session's own pins on an install where every write fails, which
is exactly where they are all that is left.

* Rebase a connected-pin drag commit on the stored list

The toggle now reads the record before changing it, but the drag commit still
wrote this window's order wholesale, so a pin another window added after the
drag began and before its storage event arrived was erased. Nothing echoes a
window's own write back to it, so there was no event left to restore it, unlike
the cancel path, which writes nothing and heals when the pending event lands.

The commit rebases: this window owns the order of the rows it dragged, the
record owns which ids are pinned, so another window's additions come in at the
front where a new pin goes and anything it unpinned stays unpinned. The
rebased list is also returned to the store, since the window has to match what
it just wrote. Unavailable storage still reads as null and leaves the order
alone, keeping pins session-only.

* Drop the row menu's connection entry and the context chip

The row menu is about the model, and Connection settings was a second way into
the destination the group heading's own gear already opens. A row with no
heading over it keeps saying which connection it came from through its logo
and tooltip; its settings are reachable from Settings then Connections.

The context window leaves the rows too. The exact count stays in Model info,
which is where a figure worth comparing belongs; a chip on every row read as
noise beside the names. formatContextLength and the marks field went with it,
having no other caller, while the catalogue plumbing that publishes the window
stays for the info box.

* Start connected names under the section labels, drop the pinned logos

Three things on the Connected rows.

Names now start where a heading's label does. 8.5 plus the row's own
pl-[5.5px] is 14, so the name lands at 14 + 14 for the leading slot + 4 for
its margin = 32px, which is the heading's px-2.5 plus a size-3.5 icon plus
gap-2. At ml-2.5 every name sat 1.5px right of the title above it. The shell's
right edge is the container's, so the action gutter does not move.

The pinned rows lose their connection logo. Down the pinned group it read as a
second glyph column before the names, and a row is there to carry its name;
which connection it came from is still on the row's own tooltip. That leaves
ModelRow's leadingSlot with no caller, so it goes too.

And that tooltip opens to the right. This panel is docked to the model button
at the window's left edge, so a row's left edge is about 30px in and a tooltip
opening that way ran off screen. Narrower with it, and breaking on words
rather than anywhere: max-w-xs let a long connection name stretch the box to
320px, most of it slack beside the model id.

* Match the Connected headings to On Device, and tighten the row pill

The Connected headings carried pt-5 and gap-2 where ListLabel, which the On
Device sections use, carries pt-3 and gap-1.5. So that list began 8px lower
than the other tab's and held its label 2px further from its icon. Both now
take ListLabel's values.

The leading slot goes with them. It held a format dot's worth of space ahead
of every connected name for a dot those rows never have, and once the pinned
logo left there was nothing in it at all: 23.5px of empty pill in front of
each name, which is the space this was about. The row's own pl-2.5 is the
name's inset now, and ml-5 plus that is 30px, where a heading's label starts
under the new gap. The prop had no other caller, so it is gone from ModelRow.

Worth saying: the collapse chevrons were already the same on both tabs, the
same lucide icon at size-3 in a 20px box. What differed was the 8px of height
above them, fixed here, and their horizontal position, which is deliberate:
the Connected heading's -mr-2 puts the chevron in the column the row buttons
below it use, rather than 8px inside it as ListLabel leaves it.

* Drop the model's own settings from the connected info box

The gear beside it opens those three fields and prints what each holds, so the
info box repeating them was a read-only second copy of that dialog. It reports
what the model is now, and keeps no id to key the per-model memories on.

* Widen the connected row pill's left inset

ml-4 with pl-3.5 still sums to the 30px a heading's label starts at, so the
name keeps its place and the extra 4px comes off the pill's left edge.

* Fix connected model settings and pin state transitions

* Drop the connected audio mark, and open the deep link after a failed sync too

The attachment adapter resolves the active model out of the loaded local ones,
so it rejects every audio file under a connected selection whatever a catalogue
publishes. The glyph is withheld and the filter drops its Audio option, which
could only ever have returned an empty list. The info box still reports the
model's published modalities, which is a fact about the model rather than an
offer.

And providersReady is set when the first sync fails as well as when it lands: a
backend that never answers left the gear opening nothing at all, where before it
opened the hydrated copy.

* Test the context window's behaviour rather than its source text

Two of the checks covering the context window assert that a line of source is
present rather than that anything happens, and one of them is the only guard on
the backend change at all.

Deleting the whole `limit.context` block from `_trim_models_dev_model` leaves
the backend suite green: no Python test covers it, because
`test_models_dev_catalog_is_trimmed_and_remapped` builds its fixture without a
`limit` key, so every entry it compares is unaffected either way. The only thing
that noticed was a TypeScript test reading the .py file as text and matching a
regex against it.

- Backend: a parametrised test over the `limit` shapes that must and must not
  yield a window, including the bool case, since `True` is an `int` greater than
  zero and would otherwise be emitted as a context length. Plus one test that the
  field survives `trim_models_dev_catalog` and that neither `limit.input` nor
  `limit.output` is mistaken for it. 20 tests to 33; deleting the block again
  fails 3 of them.
- Frontend: the served-catalogue merge and the Codex alias now drive
  `resolveModelCatalogEntry` and read the window back, which is what the info
  panel shows. The regexes they replace would have passed with those lines in
  code that never ran, and failed on a rename that changed nothing.

No production code changed. Frontend 7,829 tests, typecheck, eslint and the
backend suite all clean.

* Cut the comment bulk on the two new picker files

Post-convergence comment pass over the files this PR adds that sat furthest over
the 15% comment-to-code target: connected-model-meta.ts at 54.7% (35 of 64 lines)
and pinned-connected-models.ts at 28% (42 of 150).

Multi-line rationale collapsed to the one line carrying the fact. Every
load-bearing reason is kept: marks come from the request path rather than the
name, `modelId` is the provider's id and not the `external::` one, the audio
adapter only resolves loaded local models, nothing connected serves video through
the chat route, an external id's "::" collides with the On Device store's
repoId/quant separator, `storedPinned()` returning null is distinct from [], and
a drag owns row order while the record owns membership.

Comments only, AST-verified: 2/2 files report code unchanged. 7,829 frontend
tests, typecheck and eslint on both files clean.

unsloth: modernize account settings and show signed-in identity (#11244)

* studio: modernize account settings and show signed-in identity

* studio: refine account icons and menu width

* Keep a one-time setup code dismissable, and never invent a creation date

Two defects in the rewritten Accounts tab, each with a regression test that
fails without the fix.

perform() holds busy across the mutation AND the account refresh that follows
it, but the setup code is on screen as soon as the mutation resolves. Gating
closeEditor on busy therefore left the plaintext one-time credential with no
exit at all whenever that refresh was slow or the backend unreachable: Done was
disabled, Escape and the overlay routed through the same guard, and the dialog
sets showCloseButton false. Hiding a code is display state, not a mutation, so
dismissal no longer waits on the refresh. A code issued by an in-flight create
is still not lost: showSetup reopens the dialog when the request lands.

new Date(null) is the epoch, not an invalid date, so the NaN check alone
rendered a confident Jan 1, 1970 for an account whose created_at came back
null. It can come back null: the column is added nullable on upgrade and
_backfill_account_columns skips rows that already carry an account_id, while
_public_account passes the value straight through. Only a non-empty string now
becomes a Date; everything else falls to the dash the guard already had.

* Translate the new Accounts strings into every locale

The rewritten tab added ten keys to en.ts only, so npm run i18n:check:strict
failed with 110 missing keys across the eleven overlays. That step gates the
frontend workflow, and everything behind it -- typecheck, unit tests, build and
all twenty Playwright browser smokes -- was being skipped rather than passing.

The same change re-worded four English labels, Active to Enabled, Inactive to
Disabled, Deactivate to Disable and Reactivate to Enable, and left the overlays
translating the old wording. Parity cannot see that: the keys exist and the
placeholders match, so a German owner read Aktiv and Inaktiv against an English
UI reading Enabled and Disabled. Those four are re-translated alongside the ten.

* Tighten the two rationale comments in the accounts tab

Studio: stop the false "Failed to refresh models" error during a desktop update (#11224)

* Studio: silence model refresh toast while desktop update stops the backend

* Studio: only silence transport failures during desktop update, add test

* Studio: latch the update flag at issue and silence the documents poll too

Studio: stop the overlay rail clipping card shadows in dark mode (#11260)

* Studio: stop the overlay rail clipping card shadows in dark mode

The bottom-right rail scrolls, so it clips at its padding box, and the
12px it reserved on the inline axis was shorter than the dark-mode card
shadow reaches. 0 8px 28px -6px paints about 22px past a card's left
edge and 14px above it, so the halo ended on a hard vertical line a few
pixels out instead of fading.

Widen the gutter to 28px on the left and 20px on the top, the two edges
where a cut can be seen, and sit the rail flush against the right and
bottom edges so the clip there lands on the screen edge. The cards keep
their 16px inset and their height band: the cap grows by the gutters
that pay for them.

* Studio: keep the overlay rail's scrollport inside the viewport

Paying for the top gutter with a cap past 100dvh put the rail's
scrollport top at -4px, so once the rail scrolls, a card brought back
with scrollIntoView could align 4px above the window and lose its first
pixels. That also trips the reach check in
tests/studio/playwright_update_banner_layout.py.

Take the gutter to 16px and cap the rail at 100dvh instead. The cards'
band is the same 100dvh less 32 they always had, the top gutter still
clears the 14px the dark shadow reaches above a card, and the rail
never extends past the window on any edge.

Studio: give whisper.cpp its own update notification switch (#11261)

* Studio: give whisper.cpp its own update notification switch

Settings > General > Notifications had one switch over a banner that
announces both components, so turning off llama.cpp updates also
silenced whisper.cpp and the other way round. The two ship on their own
schedules, and a machine that never transcribes audio has no use for
one of them.

Add a second pref, keyed per component, and mute the banner by the
component the card names. Both default to on, the new key is cleared by
Reset all local preferences, and the row is in the settings search
index with strings for every locale.

* Studio: hold the update card's switch across a chained apply

A chained apply renames the card when the llama.cpp phase lands and the
whisper.cpp phase starts, so the live switch flipped mid-job: with
llama.cpp notifications on and whisper.cpp off, accepting the update
took the running card, progress bar and all, off screen for the whole
second phase.

Hold the switch the card started under until the job is over, error
included, so a failed phase keeps its retry reachable. A card that was
muted before the job started stays muted.

* Studio: show the whisper.cpp offer when llama.cpp notifications are off

The backend names llama.cpp whenever it is behind, so with llama.cpp
notifications off, whisper.cpp on and both builds stale the card was
muted and the whisper.cpp update the user did ask about never showed.

Pick the component the card shows from the switches: the name the
backend gave, unless its switch is off and the other one has an offer
the user allows. The whisper line then comes off the sub-status, which
the parsed status now carries, so the version pair and the download
size are whisper's own. Update installs both either way.

* Studio: pick the update card's offer per component, both ways

Two gaps in the switch-aware card. The backend names whisper.cpp
whenever llama.cpp's release is current, so a llama.cpp backend
migration offered next to a stale whisper.cpp build was named
whisper.cpp: with whisper.cpp muted and llama.cpp on, the card the user
had asked for went missing. And the job's to_tag is the llama.cpp build
by definition, so a card showing the whisper.cpp offer announced
"whisper.cpp updated to <llama tag>".

Swap in both directions, and carry both offers on the parsed status so
the card reads its own release pair, download size and version line off
the component it shows. The finished update reports the release its own
card advertised.

Studio: search the shortcut list by pressing the chord (#11256)

* Studio: search the shortcut list by pressing the chord

Finding a shortcut meant knowing what it is called. The list is 55 actions long,
so "which one owns ⌥⌘E" was a read-every-row job.

The search box now takes a second mode, on a toggle in the field: press a chord
and the list narrows to what answers to it. Pressing the key alone is the useful
case, so a press matches any chord carrying at least what was held. O finds ⇧⌘O,
⌥⌘O and ⌥⇧⌘O; ⇧⌘O keeps the two with the Shift and drops ⌥⌘O.

The listener is capture phase, like the recorder's: bubble phase hands Escape to
the dialog first, which closes it instead of clearing the search. Escape now
backs out a step at a time, the chord then the mode, and the dialog only closes
once neither is holding it. Keys read through bindingFromEvent rather than
event.code, so the fallback for an engine that reports no code covers Tab and
Escape here too.

Covered three ways: the matcher in the node suite, the wiring by source text, and
the ordering in the settings browser harness, which is the only place the Escape
bug was visible.

The chord was hardcoded to Meta. bindingFromEvent drops a Meta chord off macOS
outright, so on the ubuntu runner the box recorded nothing and the check failed on

because Escape is what backs out of the box. The recorder can free Escape since it

where the query matches its "Esc" cap, and Shift+Escape stays searchable. The matcher
test now says it is the matcher it covers, not the box.

The rationale claimed this catches an action whose app registration disappears. It

The composer's own keydown runs before the window listener and calls

Re-approve the four unsloth-zoo findings that 2026.9.5 reopened (#11240)

Security audit is red on main: pip scan-packages :: hf-stack reports 2 CRITICAL
and 2 HIGH unbaselined, all of them first-party unsloth-zoo code that has been
reviewed and approved before. Reproduced locally by scanning the package alone,
which gives the same four.

All four are the scanner matching our own defences and idioms:

  vision_utils.py  Harvests env vars + network. The env var is
                   UNSLOTH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URL_FETCH, the opt-in gate on the SSRF
                   guard, and the network line is the requests session the guard
                   protects.
  vision_utils.py  IMDS + network. "metadata.google.internal" is in the guard's
                   BLOCKLIST. The file is flagged for refusing to fetch IMDS.
  compiler.py      Obfuscation + exec. A dynamic __import__ of a model module,
                   plus the training banner, whose chr(92) backslashes draw the
                   sloth.
  mlx/loader.py    Obfuscation + exec. A dynamic __import__, plus mx.eval, which
                   is MLX forcing evaluation of a lazy array and has nothing to
                   do with Python eval.

Two of them did not change at all. compiler.py and mlx/loader.py carry the same
evidence hashes the baseline already holds, bdfae4c24572 and cf9c8ed7bf9c; they
reopened because their file_sha256 pins no longer match a file the release
touched elsewhere. The two vision_utils findings do have new evidence hashes.

Pinned, not unpinned. I first added these without a digest, which is what the
scanner writes, and tests/security/test_scan_packages.py rejected it:
test_context_dependent_unsloth_zoo_findings_are_digest_pinned says the approval
has to be for the file as reviewed rather than for the matched lines, because an
unpinned entry would suppress the finding whatever the file later contains. The
digests are of the files as they ship in the 2026.9.5 sdist.

Verified: scan_packages.py unsloth-zoo exits 0 with nothing unbaselined, and
tests/security/ has the same 12 failures on this branch as on main, with an empty
diff between the two lists. Those 12 are this venv's broken `import unsloth`,
not related to the baseline.

repos.name: openai/codex
repos.description: Lightweight coding agent that runs in your terminal

commits.message:
Remove `com.apple.runningboard` from Seatbelt platform defaults (#46532)

GitOrigin-RevId: 746bc891b26813edfff339637400d519198708d9

Preserve request-level reasoning effort for memory and title workers (#46531)

## Why

Memory consolidation and ephemeral title generation need to use their selected request-level reasoning effort even when managed settings enable reasoning-effort overrides.

## What changed

- Exempt current and legacy memory consolidation sessions and ephemeral `thread_title` threads from reasoning-effort overrides.
- Tag temporary title threads with `thread_title` and keep them excluded from agents overview refreshes. Recap threads retain the `system` tag.
- Preserve override behavior for persisted `thread_title` threads and other ephemeral threads.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage to verify request effort, omission of effort updates from exempt workers' requests, preservation of inherited history, title thread tagging, and overview filtering.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8dbc2eb13509f9c80f90d5798a56ea33fad2a0bc

Gate reasoning effort updates on explicit model support (#46530)

## Why

Using Responses Lite does not establish whether a model accepts reasoning-effort `configuration_update` items. Unsupported models need to use the selected request-level effort, including when resuming history containing saved updates.

## What changed

- Add `supports_reasoning_effort_updates` model metadata, defaulting to `false`.
- Require the override feature, an OpenAI provider, and explicit model support for reasoning effort updates, independently of `use_responses_lite`.
- Filter saved configuration updates from unsupported requests without changing persisted history.
- Clear the pinned effort baseline when sampling with an unsupported model so returning to a supported model establishes a fresh baseline. Compaction uses the selected effort without clearing the pin.

## Testing

Add coverage for supported models with either Responses mode, unsupported-model history filtering over HTTP and WebSocket, switching to an unsupported model and back, and compaction versus sampling pin behavior. Verify missing capability metadata defaults to `false`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 8a0fbc141964bd854dbcdd6f31e1c8e97697cf22

Allow compatible feature overrides when starting the shared daemon (#46529)

## Why

Feature overrides previously forced embedded mode even when they could work with the shared daemon. A running daemon can also have different feature settings from the current invocation, including when the invocation uses defaults.

## What changed

- Allow selected Boolean feature overrides and `suppress_unstable_features_warning` in daemon mode. Keep explicit overrides that disable shared services in embedded mode.
- Pass shared-service feature overrides to newly launched daemons and persist them for restarts and updates without changing a running daemon's settings.
- Check daemon feature settings with `experimentalFeature/list` before attaching. Warn and fall back to embedded mode on mismatches, failed checks, or an incompatible code-mode host fallback policy. Skip this check for the agents overview.
- Resolve worktree configuration before daemon selection and allow worktree sessions to auto-start the daemon.
- Forward `suppress_unstable_features_warning` in thread configuration overrides.

## Testing

Add coverage for override eligibility and precedence, launch-feature persistence and reuse, and TUI fallback warnings for feature and host-policy mismatches. Extend worktree integration coverage to exercise daemon auto-start and warning suppression.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68c316f74843b1dfd8fa39bdb48bd1f649fee57f

Bind executor plugin measurements to the trusted plugin version (#46528)

## Why

Identical script contents across plugin versions do not establish that the same measurement declaration applies. Resolving measurements through generic command attribution could use a different version's declaration, while shared helper paths could make attribution ambiguous.

## What changed

- Match canonical executor paths against trusted plugin identities before comparing script contents. Require an exact version match for measurements while retaining attribution across versions with matching contents.
- Keep measurement declarations bound to the selected trusted root, and allow distinct versions to coexist when extending trusted roots.
- Add `PluginMeasurementTarget` to extract an untrusted plugin/version hint from canonical remote cache paths, respecting Windows and POSIX path conventions.
- Skip executor lookups for unrelated scripts so attribution does not wait for executor provisioning.
- Increase the login unit test timeout in Bazel to `long`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for multiple plugins and versions, canonical aliases, symlink escapes, path casing, and executor lookup avoidance. Add a remote execution integration test verifying that mismatched versions retain command attribution but receive no metrics sidecar, and matching versions use the trusted measurement declaration.

GitOrigin-RevId: d63430b37bf2de360c8d09af7f7453a5b5024d72

Pin WinGet publishing dependencies in the release workflow (#46527)

## Why

The WinGet Releaser action references `cargo-binstall@main`, violating the requirement for full commit SHA action pins.

## What changed

Replace the action with explicit steps that install SHA-pinned `cargo-binstall` version `1.23.0` and `komac` version `2.16.0`. Discover the published Windows archive URLs and require two matching assets before submitting the `OpenAI.Codex` update.

Use `komac` to sync the publishing fork, submit the WinGet update, and clean up merged branches.

GitOrigin-RevId: da4da51937a372b841f42420b5bf775a9c151e4e

Retry busy executable launches in packaged daemon tests (#46524)

## Why

Freshly copied executables can briefly remain busy on Linux CI workers, causing packaged daemon tests to fail at launch.

## What changed

Retry the command launch in `packaged_daemon_launch` up to twice on `std::io::ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy`, waiting 10 ms between attempts. Other launch errors still propagate immediately.

GitOrigin-RevId: afb6213173a7ae4bcfe2e1e6fab6ced65ab5bf77

Default local binding to true for MXC managed networking (#46523)

## Why

MXC's native host-loopback access is bidirectional, so it cannot enforce `allow_local_binding = false`. Treating an omitted setting as `false` prevents managed networking from working with the default configuration.

## What changed

- Preserve an omitted `allow_local_binding` until the executor's sandbox policy is known. Default to `true` for Windows MXC and `false` elsewhere, including remote execution.
- Reject an effective `false` for MXC managed networking after applying policy restrictions, without enabling disabled networking.
- Use the executor's resolved value for remote network approval decisions while preserving explicit controller restrictions.
- Document that local binding permits local servers and direct host-loopback connections and skips additional private-network destination checks; proxy domain rules still apply.

## Testing

Add coverage for per-executor defaults, explicit values, MXC rejection of `false`, and remote network review cleanup with the resolved policy.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0fa7c1eaec68bebada2b8f7af45688315eea70a9

Enable Guardian parent-compaction reuse by default (#46522)

## What changed

Promote `guardian_reuse_parent_compaction` to stable and enable it by default, allowing Guardian to reuse encrypted parent compaction when restarting review sessions.

## Testing

Update Guardian tests to rely on the default setting, including evidence retention after compaction and resume. Adjust cache-key assertions to verify that parent-history changes invalidate cached review sessions by default, while explicitly disabling reuse preserves the previous behavior.

GitOrigin-RevId: 196aff1e91d022490b3782f6c7b5f168907efab9

Use macOS member fallback in shared process-group termination helpers (#46521)

## Why

On macOS, process-group signals can be denied even when individual members can be signalled. Core execution cleanup used helpers that did not retry those signals against group members.

## What changed

- Make `terminate_process_group` and `kill_process_group` use the existing member fallback on macOS, and simplify MCP and pipe callers to use the shared helpers.
- Use the saved process-group ID when escalating cancellation after the termination grace period, so this path also uses the fallback.
- Update the unsafe process-group ID test to exercise `terminate_process_group`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 1bab28d3d53cd401b51ffe71d41fbece12aed66d

Use paused time in sampler and model catalog timeout tests (#46519)

## Why

Timeout tests can avoid waiting for real deadlines by advancing Tokio's clock, but automatic advancement can expire requests before they reach the mock server.

## What changed

Pause Tokio time in the stalled-header sampling and model catalog deadline tests. Keep polling until the mock server receives each request, then explicitly advance past the relevant timeout. Add bounded wall-clock waits and fail if a request completes before reaching the server.

Preserve assertions for sampling retry exhaustion, connection permit recovery, and the catalog's `RequestTimeout` error.

GitOrigin-RevId: 252be25d75d73c713a4b8ccac1ff20ad820df556

Handle delayed process startup in the Guardian network approval test (#46518)

## Why

Process startup can outlast the first `exec_command` yield, causing the network approval test's fixed response sequence to route a Guardian response to the parent request.

## What changed

Match mock responses by request role and call ID, and poll running sessions with `write_stdin` until final output is available. Check the allow and deny outcomes against that final output while preserving the action-routing assertions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2ea31d1bfd5a46adc6561580783e916dfab15996

Stabilize the TUI exit interruption test (#46517)

## Why

The test launches a real shell, but its fixture uses a working directory that does not exist on clean runners. Waiting only for a turn-start notification also does not establish that the shell is running before interruption.

## What changed

- Give `exit_interrupts_before_requesting_shutdown` a temporary working directory.
- Replace the fixed 30-second sleep with a loop that stays alive while a temporary directory exists, with cleanup allowing the command to finish if the test fails early.
- Wait for both the turn ID and `exit-test-ready` output within a single 10-second timeout, and fail immediately if the turn completes before interruption.

GitOrigin-RevId: d8f92b941b3fe8a077f447c6bf705a2ef922db03

Handle completion timing in the multi-agent resume test (#46516)

## Why

A grandchild's completion can arrive while the worker is completing its response, triggering an extra sampling request to drain the message. The cold root resume test previously allowed only one worker completion request.

## What changed

Match worker completion requests by the nested spawn's `function_call_output` and allow one or two requests. Scope the mock to the initial worker's lifetime and drop it before the follow-up phase.

GitOrigin-RevId: 10e0a429e6e1f51b5f04a86e3351c5fa4df9cb66

Replay guardian checkpoints into a fresh session in tests (#46514)

## Why

Replaying a checkpoint into the original session can let preserved live state
mask missing checkpoint data.

## What changed

Update `guardian_checkpoint_preserves_live_context_without_storage` to restore
forked history into a fresh session with the matching guardian context mode.
Keep the existing context restoration assertions for both `Legacy` and
`ThreadOwned` modes.

GitOrigin-RevId: 211b567f6b33ffca6dc51110a208aec234004b98

Rename `AgentControl` to `LocalAgentControl` (#46513)

GitOrigin-RevId: a8e8a5c818a1751c5d2667f5af87e481482fc7db

Capture Guardian review checkpoints from live context (#46512)

## Why

Committing a Guardian review snapshot currently flushes and reloads the transcript from storage, even though the completed model context is already available in memory.

## What changed

- Build forkable checkpoints directly from live session state, preserving model history, retained Guardian context, world state, turn context, and token usage.
- Preserve compaction window metadata and MCP resource origins in the checkpoint.
- Recognize prior user turns inside compacted replacement history.

## Testing

Add round-trip checkpoint tests for legacy and thread-owned Guardian context without storage, including preservation after live history is mutated. Extend the review compaction test to assert that checkpoints do not load history from storage.

GitOrigin-RevId: cb2638ca93bba6ab4472de50c7e2913e1a2f25a8

Avoid cloning excluded turn items during thread resume (#46511)

## Why

Resuming a running thread with a summary initial page cloned every active-turn item before discarding those outside the summary, including potentially large reasoning payloads.

## What changed

- Snapshot the active turn using the requested `TurnItemsView`, copying only the first user message and final agent message for summaries and no items for `NotLoaded`.
- Preserve full snapshots when the resume response includes full turns, even if its initial page requests a summary.
- Share item selection between snapshots and page responses, and skip selection when a turn already has the requested view.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for summary selection, completed-turn metadata, and metadata-only snapshots. Extend running-thread resume coverage for default summaries, explicit full pages, and full turns returned alongside a summary page.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ddcd93c44dbc8083827ac82f442b31730a4edde

Avoid cloning active turn items for metadata-only thread resumes (#46510)

## Why

Resuming a running thread cloned the active turn's items even when the response did not need them.

## What changed

Add a metadata-only turn snapshot and use it for resume status checks and initial pages with `TurnItemsView::NotLoaded`. Only snapshot items when including turns or requesting an initial page with items, preserving item data for `Summary` and `Full` views.

## Testing

Add lifecycle coverage for metadata snapshots and extend running-thread resume tests to check metadata-only responses and populated `Summary` and `Full` pages.

GitOrigin-RevId: 281a2b7e1faf3a3fc07e007a065b16235eda08b6

Flush completed Guardian reviews before delivering decisions (#46509)

## Why

The parent could receive a Guardian decision before the review's terminal event was flushed, allowing the reviewed action to start while completion was still being saved.

## What changed

Flush the review transcript and `TurnComplete` event together before delivering completion to the parent. Clear the reviewer's active turn before delivery so the parent can immediately request another review. Skip redundant completion flushes for Guardian reviewers while retaining the existing pre-completion flush on errors and cancellation.

## Testing

Add a gated thread-store regression test covering two consecutive reviews in the same reviewer thread. Verify that each save includes `TurnComplete` and that the approved command cannot start while the save is blocked.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9274b08ddba1ea93d4fb4709bbfdc2ccaea866ab

Refresh the model catalog before turns after auth changes (#46508)

## Why

Credential changes can leave the in-memory model catalog associated with a different identity, causing subsequent turns to use bundled model metadata instead of the active credentials' catalog.

## What changed

- Refresh mismatched catalogs before user turns and mailbox-triggered wakeups, resolving lazy command credentials before comparing identities.
- Reuse a matching cache or fetch models with a five-second deadline covering auth resolution and cache access. Preserve fallback behavior on failure or timeout; static catalogs need no refresh.
- Recheck the active turn after discovery so an interrupted wakeup does not continue starting a turn.

## Testing

Add coverage for user and mailbox turns after credential rotation, including switching back after another identity replaces the shared catalog. Verify refreshed context windows and request behavior, fallback on discovery failure or auth timeout, and command-auth token rotation.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7e4ad25f1c4476e2023225731924af28c1181767

Run Windows sandbox tests exclusively when local (#46507)

## Why

Sandbox setup rotates machine-wide account passwords. The process-local test lock cannot prevent concurrent `exec-server` elevated filesystem tests from changing those passwords between setup and logon.

## What changed

- Add the Bazel `exclusive-if-local` test tag to `windows-sandbox-rs` to prevent this overlap during local test execution.
- Include the full error chain and sandbox log when the elevated non-TTY command test fails to spawn a session.

GitOrigin-RevId: bba87fc606ea60a35cf0451ed0ef68ef2eb14d3a

Share ChatGPT cookies between HTTP and WebSocket transports (#46506)

## Why

WebSocket handshakes did not reuse the HTTP cookie store or retain response cookies, so routing cookies such as `__oailb` were unavailable to subsequent connections.

## What changed

- Reuse the HTTP factory's ChatGPT cookies for secure WebSocket handshakes, preserving explicit `Cookie` headers and marking generated headers sensitive.
- Retain allowlisted infrastructure cookies from both successful and rejected upgrades. Keep configured cookies scoped to their factory and exclude account and session cookies from the shared store.
- Apply HTTPS cookie scope to `wss` requests, preserving host and path restrictions and excluding insecure `ws` requests and non-ChatGPT hosts.

## Testing

Add HTTP/WebSocket cookie-sharing coverage and local TLS handshake tests for routing-cookie reuse across connectors, rejected-upgrade refreshes, explicit header precedence, cookie scope, session-cookie exclusion, and deletion.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6bd6afe16e97cf9758ca7ba207a4e88c969497a4

Support catalog parameter schemas for Multi-Agent V2 tools (#46505)

## What changed

Add optional JSON-encoded `parameters` to catalog tool messages and apply them to all six Multi-Agent V2 tools, including plain, namespaced, and code-mode exposure. Schema selection follows the active model, including mid-turn model changes.

Require an object schema supported by the existing `JsonSchema` subset and preserve bundled encryption annotations. Fall back to bundled parameters when overrides are missing, invalid, unsupported, or omit encrypted properties. Tool execution and argument handling remain unchanged.

## Testing

Extend integration coverage for schema overrides, fallback behavior, encryption annotations, exposure modes, and mid-turn model changes. Add a snapshot scenario exercising `list_agents` with a catalog parameter schema.

GitOrigin-RevId: 978be6d5f7e6a6865969922be5483bc697b20aca

Add six bundled TUI themes and theme-aware accents (#46504)

## What changed

- Bundle `ada`, `babbage`, `curie`, `cushman`, `dali`, and `davinci` themes for configuration and the theme picker, preserving precedence and invalid-file warnings for custom themes with the same names.
- Use `codex.accent` for active and selected controls on truecolor and 256-color terminals, retaining existing fallbacks at lower color depths.
- Honor terminal-default diff backgrounds and clear matching gutter fills, allowing `dali` and `davinci` to show diffs without background fills.
- Restrict Windows native palette fallback to `ConsoleWindowClass` so a ConPTY palette is not mistaken for the renderer's colors when OSC probing fails.

## Testing

Add tests and snapshots for theme preview, selection, cancellation, custom-theme precedence, invalid-file warnings, accent color depth, and disabling individual diff fills.

GitOrigin-RevId: 72f3ef08f82626436dd2d80d40210cc77e1a5616

Use catalog model display names throughout the TUI (#46503)

## Why

Model pickers and session details show raw model IDs even when the catalog provides a display name.

## What changed

- Use catalog display names in model and reasoning pickers, session headers, status displays, and terminal titles, retaining fallback labels for models absent from the catalog.
- Keep model IDs for selection and persistence, and preserve picker highlights by ID when display names change or are shared by multiple models.
- Remove the legacy-model instruction from the full model picker.

## Testing

Add regression tests and snapshots for custom display names, startup and resumed session headers, fallback labels, terminal titles, and picker refreshes. Verify that selecting a display name still persists the original model ID.

GitOrigin-RevId: 101fe82b20f7a8a90ceeff7999bd07ad42ca46db

Add configuration and feature diagnostics to report metadata (#46501)

## What changed

- Record an explicit allowlist of scalar configuration values and individual boolean feature tags for each sampling request, replacing the combined enabled-feature list.
- Distinguish configured context-window overrides from the effective model limit, and emit `unset` for absent values so earlier overrides do not linger.
- Expand `tags_json` into report metadata and raise the tag limit from 64 to 512, while allowing existing values to update at capacity.

## Testing

Add tests for configured and effective context windows, clearing overrides, feature toggles, dynamic tag upload serialization, and updates at the tag limit.

GitOrigin-RevId: 57608fac936d8ce315e36d452a2950e46370b39b

Block mutating fcntls in restricted macOS Seatbelt policies (#46500)

## Why

`F_MAKECOMPRESSED` and `F_TRANSFEREXTENTS` can mutate files through read-only descriptors, bypassing `file-write*` and `file-ioctl` restrictions. Even a deny-default Seatbelt policy needs an explicit denial for these operations.

## What changed

Deny `system-fcntl` commands `80` and `110` whenever the filesystem sandbox policy lacks full disk write access.

## Testing

Add macOS regression tests that run Seatbelt children under read-only and workspace-write policies, assert both operations fail with `EPERM`, and verify file contents and metadata remain unchanged. An unrestricted positive control verifies the mutations, allowing for unsupported extent transfers.

GitOrigin-RevId: 7a7a5ef30f9ff658a86071b51f1f7b4952d5cdad

Allow approved escalation with environment-owned network policies (#46499)

## Why

Environment-owned network policies rejected explicit sandbox escalation before command approval, and retained terminals that bypassed or no longer matched those policies required a new terminal.

## What changed

- Allow `require_escalated` commands through the normal approval flow and bypass managed network proxies when full escalation is permitted.
- Preserve denied-read restrictions, including the sandbox and network proxy needed to enforce them.
- Track the network restrictions bypassed at launch and require escalation review for terminal input when launch permissions or network settings warrant it, instead of rejecting input outright.

## Testing

Extend network approval coverage for approved and denied escalation, unproxied remote execution, and preserved denied-read restrictions. Add retained-terminal coverage verifying command and `write_stdin` approvals with restricted and unrestricted filesystems, and update the unit test for changed environment network policies to expect escalation review.

GitOrigin-RevId: 50524b1bc4e3df58447c3c92fb9e50e69ed50cf8

Allow worktree sessions to use an existing local daemon (#46498)

## Why

`--worktree` and command-line worktree feature overrides previously excluded sessions from using the local daemon, even though worktree allocation is client-owned and thread requests already forward the feature.

## What changed

- Allow `--worktree` and boolean `features.worktrees` overrides to remain eligible for daemon connections, while preserving exclusions for other configuration overrides and `--no-daemon`.
- Skip daemon auto-start for `--worktree` launches.

## Testing

Add daemon eligibility tests for worktree options and overrides. Run the existing worktree startup and fork test scenarios against both embedded and daemon backends, checking ownership before the first turn and confirming daemon connections through `/status`.

GitOrigin-RevId: b3f4782e83d8e20974fb4a831442cae013d58e56

Preserve the provisioned macOS CLI's code-signing identity (#46495)

## Why

Existing login-keychain access rules identify the CLI as `codex`. Packaging it in an app bundle must preserve that code-signing identifier independently of the bundle identifier and provisioned App ID.

## What changed

- Sign the provisioned CLI with the identifier `codex`, retaining `com.openai.codex.cli` as its bundle identifier.
- Require the expected signing identifier and team during signature verification, and reject unexpected bundle identifiers, executable names, or package types.
- Document the identity distinction and keychain compatibility limits.

## Testing

Extend signing-driver tests to check the signing identifier, verification requirement, bundle metadata, and provisioned entitlements, and to reject altered bundle identity fields. These tests use generated credentials and stubbed native tools; they do not verify runtime keychain access or credential recovery.

GitOrigin-RevId: ab00072e48189551adb0e70008210fee6d36241d

Keep remote workspace roots under server control (#46494)

## Why

Workspace paths from the client configuration belong to the client host. Sending them to a remote app server can override the server's workspace roots.

## What changed

- Omit client-configured `runtimeWorkspaceRoots` from remote start, resume, and fork requests so the server resolves defaults or restores saved roots.
- Preserve server-provided roots when forking an active session or side conversation, including after reloading client configuration.
- Reject `--add-dir` and `sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots` command-line overrides with `--remote` before connecting, directing users to configure additional roots on the server.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for remote workspace roots across start, turn, resume, and fork operations; active-session forks after configuration reloads; and embedded requests retaining explicit roots. CLI tests cover rejected root overrides and continued acceptance of network-access overrides.

GitOrigin-RevId: b87ea6037d197db68e25a1a8610d693f6aa13caf

Allow `/review` during MCP startup (#46493)

## Why

MCP startup alone should not prevent opening the review picker or submitting inline review instructions.

## What changed

- Defer `/review` availability checks and draft clearing to dispatch, where thread state is available.
- Reject live review commands while foreground work is running, pending, or queued, preserving the draft and attachments.
- Distinguish live and queued dispatch so a queued review does not clear a newer composer draft.

## Testing

Add regression tests for the review picker and inline instructions during MCP startup, draft and attachment preservation when review is blocked, and newer draft preservation when a queued review opens.

GitOrigin-RevId: 48962bfc26127ffa8dd157f15be512b78bf9b39b

Unify TUI tool output previews with a three-row limit (#46492)

## What changed

- Use a shared preview renderer for agent command output and MCP results, showing the first three wrapped rows with a hidden-line count and `ctrl + t` transcript hint.
- Apply one preview budget across all MCP result blocks. Count partially displayed logical lines as hidden and hard-wrap long URLs to fit the available width.
- Preserve complete MCP result text in transcript and raw output, including trailing failure diagnostics.
- Bound preview input before wrapping to limit work on very long lines and combining characters.

## Testing

Add unit tests and snapshots for wrapped output, hidden-line counts, blank lines, combining characters, shared MCP block limits, transcript preservation, and matching streamed and completed command previews.

GitOrigin-RevId: bd3c2ec40ee837dc8a7a171aaf91577a0ac50985

Compose gateway OAuth with primary provider authentication (#46490)

## Why

Providers configured with `gateway_oauth` need gateway credentials alongside primary authentication for inference and model discovery.

## What changed

- Attach gateway tokens through the configured header or cookie while preserving primary authentication, including WebSocket handshake headers.
- Share gateway credential managers across matching provider instances and model discovery so they observe refreshed tokens.
- Reject authentication on gateway setup or token failures, invalid token values, and conflicting auth headers. Mark gateway headers sensitive and avoid exposing issuer error details.
- Include gateway OAuth configuration in model catalog cache identity to prevent reuse across different gateway configurations.

## Testing

Add provider and core integration tests covering combined credentials, header and cookie delivery, token refresh, shared credential state, cache isolation, and request blocking on gateway token or HTTP client initialization failures.

GitOrigin-RevId: cb74125cf7e87660967d49edacf14646cf0b99c4

Split analytics tests into focused suites (#46488)

## What changed

Replace `analytics_client_tests.rs` with event-specific suites under
`codex-rs/analytics/src/tests/suite/` and shared fixtures in `tests/support.rs`.
Group turn tests by events, requests, compaction, and accepted lines, and keep
cross-event arrival-order coverage in a dedicated reducer ordering suite.

Separate app and plugin ingestion assertions into their respective suites while
retaining a combined test for arrival order. Document where to place tests based
on the contract they cover.

GitOrigin-RevId: aba497f103ad6e23eca6266fc93d150d16f5913c

Keep TUI exploration grouped across reasoning and nonzero exits (#46487)

## Why

Reasoning summaries and nonzero command exits split adjacent exploration into separate groups, while compact history omitted exit codes. Replayed commands also failed to retain the same grouping as live commands.

## What changed

- Keep adjacent read, list, and search commands grouped across reasoning summaries and nonzero exits in both live and replayed history.
- Preserve reasoning in chronological order in the expanded transcript while omitting it from compact and raw history.
- Show nonzero exit codes in compact exploration entries and keep unsuccessful reads separate from successful read summaries. Render search exit code `1` without red failure styling, and label compound-command outcomes as `command exit`.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for live/replay rendering parity, reasoning order, grouping boundaries, and nonzero exit labels and colors. Update the overlapping-command test to verify that exploration stays grouped after a failure.

GitOrigin-RevId: 19c6ffec44c62c185fc6f79282c38e66468f7b80

Make TUI async question replies compatible with desktop (#46486)

## Why

Async questions answered on another client should disappear from the TUI without losing drafts for other questions, even when questions have identical titles.

## What changed

- Send answers using the desktop reply envelope with stable per-question IDs, and resolve matching questions from committed messages and replayed history.
- Render replies as readable question-and-answer text in transcripts, queue previews, and input history.
- Preserve separate reply envelopes and message order when retrying rejected or interrupted input.
- Account for JSON escaping in input limits and fall back to plain text for oversized question IDs.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for cross-client dismissal, draft preservation, replay ordering, reply parsing, IDE context, distinct replies with identical text, and retry ordering. Update the async question scenario to use the reply envelope.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9b9e4b1e140508590401622d96cfc16fc192eb7c

Handle unknown error classifications and configure gateway OAuth (#46482)

Preserve known error classifications, including BioPolicy, while falling back to Other for unknown values so saved sessions can still be read.

Add optional gateway OAuth settings to model provider configuration.

Co-authored-by: Owen Lin <owen@openai.com>
Co-authored-by: alexsong-oai <alexsong@openai.com>
GitOrigin-RevId: 64bcf45ca042efca7645c798db3746375426b0fe

Keep MCP policy evaluation consistent with turn environments (#46335)

## Why

Environment settings saved for the next turn must not change MCP tool availability during the active turn.

## What changed

- Use one captured environment snapshot for MCP policy evaluation and runtime publication, including selections that are still starting or have failed.
- Compare both captured selections and ready environment handles when deciding whether to refresh the runtime, and rebuild the startup configuration when resolved selections change.
- Preserve the configuration origin of failed selections so MCP authority evaluation retains whether configuration comes from the thread.
- Box the MCP refresh future to keep it off the sampling request's stack.

## Testing

Add a regression test that updates the environment MCP policy while a turn waits for user input, verifies the tool remains visible when that turn resumes, and verifies it disappears on the next turn. Extend snapshot tests to cover starting and failed selections.

GitOrigin-RevId: cc2744b5137be69f000d70b0c7009b14079f39ae

Share platform identity across path, network, and sandbox configuration (#46334)

## What changed

- Add `Platform` to `codex-utils-path-uri` with metadata parsing, native platform detection, and path convention mapping. Preserve missing or unrecognized metadata as `Unknown`.
- Replace `NetworkProxyExecutorOs` with the shared type and keep executor-specific socket path validation in the network proxy.
- Extract `effective_sandbox_mode` with explicit platform and Windows sandbox level inputs, preserving the native Windows fallback from `workspace-write` to `read-only` when the sandbox is disabled.

## Testing

Add unit tests for platform metadata, path conventions, native platform detection, and sandbox mode selection across platforms and Windows sandbox levels.

GitOrigin-RevId: 4fe0972e3a91040e35f2a6dfa5bcdf6c9a29be88

Handle disabled Windows sandbox accounts during cleanup (#46333)

## Why

Cleanup needs fresh logon tokens for sandbox accounts that may already be disabled. Temporarily enabling those accounts must leave a durable obligation to disable them again if the service exits unexpectedly.

## What changed

- Persist `cleanup_logon_pending` before enabling an account, then disable it again after the logon attempt before clearing the marker.
- Recover pending account disables before owner restoration or IPC admission, validating account SIDs before restoration. Block runtime readiness and provisioning while recovery is pending, and defer retirement until cleanup logons are prepared.
- Include the blocking logon details in cleanup timeout errors and suppress repeated identical cleanup errors in the Windows event log.

## Testing

Add receipt tests covering backward-compatible defaults and pending cleanup state surviving serialization, blocking readiness and owner admission until cleared.

GitOrigin-RevId: 801bec408a27ac85ccdc3eb5ca2bdb2ccb3d5827

Dim conversation recaps in the TUI (#46332)

## What changed

Apply dim styling to all rendered recap lines and remove the cyan color from
`Next:`, preserving italics and bold labels.

## Testing

Update recap style assertions and add a rendered-buffer snapshot covering dimmed
text, label styling, line breaks, and next-action wrapping.

Log what the glasses were actually told, and what the Barrier then did.

feat: native menu-bar hiding on macOS 27 (direct build) (#403)

* feat: hide natively on macOS 27 in a direct (non-App Store) build

macOS 27 ejects an inflated separator from the menu bar, so length-based
hiding stops working there (#360). Add NativeVisibilityEngine: it reads which
apps the user placed in each section (Accessibility, relative to the
separators) and asks macOS to keep only the allowed apps visible through the
menu-bar visibility restriction behind assessment mode. macOS hides the rest
and reflows the bar, independent of display width, the notch and the
frontmost app's menus.

That restriction lives in MenuBarClientCore, a private framework. All use of
it sits in HBNativeVisibilityShim (Objective-C, runtime-resolved, exceptions
caught) and compiles only with HIDDENBAR_NATIVE_VISIBILITY, which the new
Debug-Direct / Release-Direct configurations set. Those configurations sign
with Hidden-Direct.entitlements (no App Sandbox): on macOS 27 the sandbox
denies the mach-lookup Accessibility needs (com.apple.axserver) even with
the permission granted, so the App Store build cannot read the sections and
keeps LegacyLengthEngine.

Measured on 27.0 before building this:
- activation works sandboxed and unsandboxed; invalidate, or process exit,
  restores the bar
- the configuration takes NSArrays; an NSSet raises
- system items are numeric ids (2 clock, 5 sound, 6 wifi, 8 control center
  on the test Mac); unknown ids up to 63 are ignored
- while a restriction is active, hidden items report stale positions, so
  sections are read only from an unrestricted bar

Behavior: collapse allows Hidden Bar plus the visible section; expand drops
the restriction, or keeps the always-hidden section hidden while "hide
separators" is on. A new restriction is activated before the old one is
dropped. Every failure (API missing, no Accessibility, activation error)
leaves the bar expanded and reports .unavailable; the controller shows it
as expanded. Separators stay at their normal width.

Limits: hiding is per app (an app's icons move together, most visible wins);
macOS's own items stay visible; an app launched while collapsed stays hidden
until the next collapse re-reads the sections.

Adds an unhosted HiddenBarTests target: layout resolver (LTR/RTL, grouping,
exclusions) and engine transitions against fake inventory and visibility.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: make the native engine responsive and tidy on real macOS 27

Found testing the direct build on 27.0:
- The Accessibility walk blocked the collapse for up to ~18s: every running
  process was queried with the default timeout, and dozens of WebKit/XPC
  helpers never answer. Query only app bundles (the only status-item
  owners seen), with a 0.1s timeout, off the main thread (~1s total).
- The separators sat idle beside the arrow while collapsed. They drop to
  zero width once hiding succeeds and return on expand (zero width rather
  than isVisible, which would forget their position).
- Log the resolved sections, and every distinct reason hiding is
  unavailable, instead of only the first.

Also measured: the allow-list matches an app's own items only for the copy
LaunchServices resolves for its bundle id, which for an installed app is the
one in /Applications. Other copies of Hidden Bar (build products, archives)
have their items hidden.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: use the arrow as the hiding boundary on macOS 27

With native hiding the separator no longer has to widen, so it only
duplicated the arrow. The native engine now reads sections relative to the
arrow (apps on its left are hidden) and keeps the regular separator at zero
width, not removed, so macOS keeps its saved position for the legacy engine.
The always-hidden separator still marks the third section while expanded.

The "is the arrangement usable" checks move from the controller into the
engines, since they depend on which item is the boundary: the legacy engine
keeps the separator-left-of-arrow rule, the native engine accepts any
arrangement and checks the always-hidden separator against the arrow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: take the unused separator out of the bar on macOS 27

Zero width still left a gap beside the arrow, since macOS pads every
status item. The native engine hides the regular separator outright, and
the controller creates the engine at launch so it never flashes on screen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: changelog and backlog for native hiding on macOS 27

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor: isolate menu-bar hiding behind engine (#402)

* fix: size a runtime-enabled always-hidden separator at its resting width

btnAlwaysHiddenLength was captured once at launch, so enabling the section
from Preferences at runtime created its separator at 0pt, invisible until
the next launch. Read the preference live instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: isolate menu-bar hiding behind engine

Move the separator-length mechanics out of StatusBarController into a
MenuBarEngine, with the existing behavior preserved in LegacyLengthEngine.
The controller keeps the status items, UI, preferences, timers and hover
handling; the engine owns how hiding is achieved. MenuBarEngineFactory is
the single place an engine is chosen, so an OS-specific mechanism (#360)
can be added without version checks spreading through the controller.

No intentional behavior change:
- collapse state stays derived from the live separator length (> 20pt),
  so it still survives a length recompute while collapsed (PR #354)
- the collapse length is still max(500, min(widest screen * 2, 10_000))
- the always-hidden separator is still inflated only by "hide separators",
  never by collapse, and is re-applied on a display change only when the
  bar was collapsed with separators hidden
- the one-shot HideMechanism diagnostic log moves into the legacy engine
  unchanged

fix(node-api): clamp pattern-wait timeout to avoid Instant+Duration overflow panic (#3538)

`EventStream::wait_for_correlation` — the shared engine behind the public
`recv_service_response` and `recv_action_result` pattern helpers — computed
an absolute deadline as `Instant::now() + timeout` from the caller-supplied
`Duration`. A very large value, e.g. `Duration::MAX` used to mean "wait
effectively forever", overflows the monotonic clock and panics with
`overflow when adding duration to instant`, aborting the whole process.

The C++ binding already guards the identical computation on the FFI side
(`clamp_pattern_timeout` in `apis/c++/node`), noting that "the pattern
helpers compute `Instant::now() + timeout` internally"; the Rust-native
callers were left unguarded.

Add a `representable_wait_deadline` helper that reads the clock once and
halves the timeout until `now + timeout` is representable, returning the
`Instant` deadline directly. A caller asking for an enormous wait now gets
the longest representable deadline instead of a crash. (`futures_timer::Delay`
already saturates a huge duration to a ~30-year deadline, so the loop body is
safe once the deadline is guarded.)

Adds a unit test asserting a normal timeout yields a near-future deadline and
`Duration::MAX` yields a future deadline rather than panicking.

Machine-generated by an automated Claude Code review agent; no human has
reviewed this change. Please review carefully before merging.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MUMG4MrFiPKiwjC8xvtH3d

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): avoid Instant+Duration overflow panic in the topic hz/echo samplers (#3537)

The non-interactive `dora topic hz` and `dora topic echo` samplers computed
their stop time as `Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(seconds)`, where
`seconds` comes directly from the `--duration` flag. clap bounds that flag only
from below (`range(1..)`), so a large-but-valid `u64` such as
`--duration 10000000000000000000` overflows the monotonic clock and panics
(`overflow when adding duration to instant`), aborting the command before it
samples anything.

Track the window as a start `Instant` plus an `elapsed()`/`saturating_sub`
comparison instead, so no `Instant + Duration` addition is performed:

- `hz`: the sampling loop now measures elapsed time directly, mirroring the
  sibling `dora topic info` sampler.
- `echo`: the per-iteration timeout / stop decision is factored into a small
  pure `echo_recv_timeout` helper that takes the already-computed `elapsed`,
  keeping the loop off `Instant + Duration` while preserving the periodic
  "enable debug inspection" hint wake-ups.

`Receiver::recv_timeout` handles an oversized remaining duration via its own
`checked_add` fallback, so the loop bodies are safe too.

Adds regression tests: `run_hz_oneshot_does_not_panic_on_oversized_duration`
drives the hz sampler with a 10^19-second window and a disconnected receiver,
and `echo_recv_timeout_does_not_panic_on_oversized_duration` pins the echo
helper's behavior across the no-duration, huge-duration, elapsed, and
shorter-than-hint cases.

the CLI --worktree layout), and a "New worktree" action in the welcome

The selector moves out of the composer footer onto the welcome row, to
the right of the branch picker, in the same chip style. It only appears
for git repos since a worktree is cut from the branch chosen next to it.
