repos.description: App which allows you to use your health devices beyond subscriptions. Supports Workout Tracking, Nutrition Tracking, Wellness Excercise, Sleep, Recovery, Strain, and Many more.

commits.message:
fix: serialize widget push() so concurrent calls can't interleave (#416)

resume, post-derive, and bg-wake all fire WidgetService.refresh->push()
unawaited with no lock. push() writes ~20 keys with an await between
each, so two overlapping calls could interleave their writes and land
a snapshot mixing fields from two different days. chain push() through
a static future so overlapping calls run strictly one after another.

fix: atomic db-backed slot allocation for notification ids (#415)

* fix: atomic db-backed slot allocation for notification ids

_slotFor was doing a plain read-then-write over shared_preferences with
no lock or transaction, so two isolates (foreground app + headless
BLE/BGTask sync) allocating for two different dedupeKeys in the same
category at the same time could both land on the same slot -> same OS
notification id -> one show() call silently replaces the other. same
bug class fired_keys.dart already fixed for the fire-once guard via an
atomic sqlite INSERT OR IGNORE, so give slot allocation the same
treatment: new notif_slots table + UNIQUE(category, slot) index,
claimNotifSlot does one atomic get-or-insert. shared_preferences kept
as a mirror + degraded-mode fallback when there's no db.

schema 53. no kAlgoVersion bump, this is notification plumbing not
analytics output.

* address review: bound probe loop, guard bandSize, log DB-fallback degrade, fix test claim

- cap maxProbes to bandSize (a stale hint could otherwise re-probe already-claimed slots up to 1024 times for no gain)
- guard bandSize <= 0 and normalize startAt % bandSize before probing
- log (not silently swallow) when the DB slot claim fails and we degrade to the SharedPreferences fallback, since that reopens the race this PR closes
- reworded notification_ids_atomic_test.dart's header/test comment: Future.wait doesn't force true SQLite-level interleaving in one isolate (the write lock serializes it), so it proves the UNIQUE-index claim is collision-free rather than reproducing the actual cross-isolate race

* fix: db-backed slot must win over a diverged prefs mirror on every read

_slotFor checked the SharedPreferences mirror BEFORE ever trying the DB
claim, so a stale/diverged prefs entry (partial write, pre-migration
leftover) would win over the DB forever after the first allocation --
the DB was only ever authoritative on first write, not on read. move
the DB claim ahead of the prefs check so it runs on every call; the
prefs existing-slot check now only applies inside the degraded
fallback (no DB in this process).

added a regression test that corrupts the prefs mirror to point at a
different slot than the DB owns and asserts the DB value wins.

fix: setThemeDark never told the watch about theme changes (#414)

push, pushBattery, and clear all call _syncWatch after writing so
WatchBridge mirrors the change. setThemeDark wrote theme_dark and
retheme'd the iOS widgets but skipped it, so a paired watch kept the
old theme until some unrelated push/pushBattery/clear happened to
fire next.

fix: workouts list distance ignores imperial unit setting (#413)

_stats() hardcoded km for imported workout distance while every other
screen (summary, live, share) uses UnitsController. now it does too.

fix: whoop import merges same-day csv files instead of clobbering (#412)

physiological_cycles.csv and sleeps.csv both classify as a day file and
both write the same date. writeDay was firing per row per file, so
sleeps.csv landing after physiological_cycles.csv (or vice versa) would
overwrite day_result/metric_series with nulls for whatever columns that
file doesn't have, silently wiping recovery/rhr/rmssd/strain or the
sleep fields depending on order.

now every file's day rows get extracted and merged per date first (new
non-null value wins, keeps prior otherwise), then written once per
date. order no longer matters.

coach: validate date in log_journal/log_period too (#411)

these two were the only date-taking tools implemented inline in
_runTool and the only ones skipping CoachActions.day() - every
sibling (log_food, log_journal_fields, add_completed_workout,
mark_medication) already routes through it. a model sending a
missing or relative date ("today"/"yesterday") got interpolated
straight into the write, silently keying a journal/cycle_log row
under a string nothing else can ever read back. for log_period
that's a real reproductive-health tracking gap.

now both call CoachActions.day() first and use the validated/
defaulted date in both the confirmation summary and the write, same
as every other tool. dropped date from required since day() already
defaults empty to today. added the description hint on the schema
sibling tools already have.

ios: stop re-arming forgotten bands on willRestoreState (#410)

willRestoreState was inserting a default ArmState() for every peripheral
CoreBluetooth handed back, even ones removed via disarm(). that made
didConnect's arms[uuid] != nil guard pass, so a lingering restored
connection for an unpaired band would get armed and wake dart into a
headless sync for a device the user forgot. cancel those directly
instead of stashing them in arms.

reject NaN lat/lng in healthkit route import (#409)

NaN.abs() > 90 is false so the existing range guard let it through.
same class of bug as the flutter_map NaN crash, route_tracker already
guards its live path with isNaN, import path didn't.

high freq wake window: fix DST-unsafe next-day arithmetic (#408)

* high freq wake window: fix DST-unsafe next-day arithmetic

Duration(days: 1) is exactly 24 elapsed hours, off by an hour across a DST
transition. matches the DateTime(y, m, d+1, h, min) pattern already used
elsewhere (alarm_schedule.dart) for the same reason. flagged by pr-agent
on #403 after that PR was already merged, so it needed its own PR.

* add regression test for the DST/calendar-arithmetic fix

pr-agent flagged the fix as untested. pins targetWake's next-day rollover
to calendar arithmetic across a month boundary, same pattern
alarm_schedule_test.dart already uses for nextAlarmOccurrence.

fix: signal priority resolver drops devices paired after custom ranking (#405)

once signal_priority had any stored row, a device that started declaring
that signal later (paired after the user customized ranking) never made it
into resolveOwnership's candidate list. its real device_coverage got
silently excluded forever, no automatic re-seed path. the "which source
wins" screen shows a merged order that looks saved but never was.

union coverage-only devices in below the stored ranking (sorted,
in-memory, never persisted, same as the empty-priority fallback). bumped
kAlgoVersion since ownership resolution output changes for anyone in this
situation.

fix: exportWorkout could double-write a workout when exportAll raced it (#404)

exportAll's day-wide WORKOUT delete-then-write and exportWorkout's
session-scoped delete-then-write both hit the same HealthExporter
singleton with no coordination. AppState's single-flight guard only
covers concurrent exportAll calls, not the unawaited exportWorkoutId
fired from endWorkout/coach/import/log_workout. if a workout ends right
as a scheduled derive-pass export runs, both deletes can find nothing
(the sibling hasn't written yet) and both writes land, so the same
workout shows up twice in Apple Health / Health Connect and every later
day-wide rewrite just preserves the duplicate.

added a small chained-future mutex on the exporter instance and
serialized exportAll, exportWorkout, and deleteWorkoutWindow's delete
through it. all five external call sites are unchanged.

mirror the foreground alarm-confirm self-heal in headless sync too (#406)

when armNextScheduledOccurrence's same-epoch dedupe returns epoch: null,
the re-arm/poll block in runHeadlessSync never runs, so a live ALARM_SET
(event 56) arriving during a headless drain had nowhere to flip
alarm_epoch_confirmed. an alarm confirmed only while the app was
backgrounded would never get marked confirmed.

smart wake: cover the armed alarm's own window, not just habitual wake (#403)

* smart wake: cover the armed alarm's own window, not just habitual wake

HighFreqWakeWindow only ever leased the sync-frequency bump around the
14-day habitual wake median, so an alarm set well before that (e.g. 05:30
on a 07:30-habitual person) never got shorter sync cadence during its own
smart window. decoded_onehz stayed on the 900s floor and _checkSmartWake's
"last 3 minutes" query usually came up short of the 30 rows it needs, so
smart wake silently never got a chance to fire early.

added armedSmartWakeWindow() to alarm_schedule.dart (dedupes the
windowEnd/weekday lookup _checkSmartWake already did inline) and threaded
it into HighFreqWakeWindow as an optional scheduled-window param that ORs
against the habitual lease. wired at both call sites (app_state + the
headless background_sync path, which now reads the schedule/alarm_epoch
before planNow instead of after). every existing call site that doesn't
pass the new params behaves exactly as before.

band's own SET_ALARM fallback untouched either way.

* fix TOCTOU flagged by pr-agent: re-read schedule/epoch after runSync

the earlier read was reused for the post-sync arm step too. runSync() is
a long BLE drain — if the user edits the alarm schedule mid-sync, the arm
step would've overwritten it with the stale pre-sync copy. now the
pre-sync read only feeds the HighFreqWakeWindow check, and the arm step
re-reads fresh, same as it did before this PR.

skin_temp_z: add the same quantum floor readiness already has (#402)

skinTempZ was gated only on sd > 0 against the raw ADC baseline. a
baseline sitting between two adjacent ADC counts has nonzero but
sub-1-count SD, so ordinary quantization noise standardized into an
inflated z. analytics already refuses this exact channel below a
1-ADC-count quantum (tempInput in readiness_composite.dart), edge just
never applied it to its own independent z. bumped kAlgoVersion, added a
test.

fix: manual hr zone bounds accepted negative/zero thresholds (#401)

ascending-only check in both the profile reader and the zones editor let
strictly-ascending garbage like -50,-20,0,40,80 through and it'd render
forever until someone noticed. added a shared floor check (kHrFloorBpm,
same one already used for sensor dropout elsewhere in this file) both
paths now route through.

fix fabricated resting-hr note on manual zones (#400)

manual zones fell into the generic !measured branch of
distributionNote, which prints "not enough nights of resting heart
rate" with have/need numbers even when the user has 28+ nights on
file. that's not why the chart is missing, manual zones just have no
measured anchor at all. gave manual its own branch (like tanaka
already has) and a real sentence for it.

fix Typed.of accepting Infinity/NaN/overflow as valid numbers (#398)

double.tryParse lets "Infinity"/"-Infinity"/"NaN" through and
overflows huge literals like 1e400 to infinity, none of which are null
so Typed.of marked them valid. every caller that then calls .round()
without an isFinite check crashes (same bug as the zone-5 upper edge
fix, just reachable from any of the 8 Typed.of text fields now,
new-zones sheet included). added the isFinite check at the shared
parser so it's fixed everywhere at once.
gate _onEngineState behind resetgate too — same bug as _onLiveEvent, different callback (#397)

fix manual hr zone crash (double.infinity.round()) (#395)

* fix: manual hr zone 5's upper edge can't be Infinity

merged in #393 with double.infinity for zone 5's open upper edge.
getZones() and the session zone-band builder both call .round() on
every zone's upper bpm unconditionally, and Infinity.round() throws
— so setting a manual zone override crashes the zones screen and any
session summary. zone 5 doesn't need infinity anyway: zoneNumber()
never checks its upper edge, only display code reads it, so it gets
the existing hard-ceiling constant instead.

* clarify: zone 5's finite value is display-only, not a classification bound

pr_agent nitpick on #395: the doc said zone 5 has no upper edge full
stop, which now reads as a contradiction next to _manualZones giving
it a real number. spelled out that the finite value is there only
because .round() can't take Infinity — zoneNumber() still never
looks at it.

fix cold-launch race in the alarm siri intent (#392 follow-up) (#396)

* fix the real coderabbit finding: cold-launch init race

_init() and checkPendingSiriRoute() were both fired unawaited from the
constructor with no ordering between them. on a fresh launch, if the
siri "enable tomorrow's alarm" flag was already set, checkPendingSiriRoute
could run setScheduleDay against the still-default (07:00, disabled)
in-memory schedule before _loadAlarmSchedule() got a chance to load the
real persisted times - clobbering whatever custom time the user had for
that weekday.

now checkPendingSiriRoute only runs (on cold launch) after _init settles.
the resume-time call site is unaffected - by then init is long done.

skipped coderabbit's other two suggestions:
- "arm failure isn't retried": setScheduleDay's arm step already
  swallows its own BLE errors and _armNextAlarmOccurrence gets called
  again on every subsequent connect/sync regardless, same as the manual
  toggle on the alarm screen. no special-casing needed, it already
  self-heals.
- "non-destructive read + single-flight guard": the only way to race
  the read+clear is two overlapping resumes, and worst case is a
  harmless duplicate setScheduleDay(enabled: true) for the same day -
  not a correctness bug worth a mutex for.

* gate the resume path too, not just the constructor's own call

sourcery caught that my last fix only covered the constructor's OWN
checkPendingSiriRoute call. app.dart's resume handler calls it directly
too, and a cold launch's first "resumed" lifecycle event can land before
_init() has loaded the real schedule just as easily as the constructor's
unawaited call could - so the same clobber-tomorrow's-time bug was still
reachable through that second call site.

moved the guard INTO checkPendingSiriRoute itself (awaits the stored
_init() future first) so both callers go through the same gate instead
of needing it duplicated at every call site.

add an honest vo2max estimate (#394)

* add an honest vo2max estimate, not the old rhr-ratio trap

discussion #360 keeps asking for vo2max. the old one got deleted because
15.3*hrmax/rhr collapses to a rescaled resting hr with no independent
signal, and it fed physiologicalAge which double-counted the same number.

this one needs an actual steady-state workout: a completed 1 km GPS split
with its own avg hr, held for 5+ min. ACSM speed->VO2, then Swain &
Leutholtz's %HRR≈%VO2R to get to max. abstains outside a genuine submax
%HRR band, on short/partial splits, or when hr_max/resting_hr are too
close to trust. backfilled once per session (like hrr_bpm/avg_hr already
are), never recomputed.

surfaced as one more row in the workout summary, same pattern as HR
recovery. null on basically every indoor session and that's correct, not
a bug.

pins analytics to f334a06 (adds vo2maxSubmaxEstimate, additive only).

* repin analytics to the coderabbit fix (grade in inputs_used)

let you set your own hr zones (#304) (#393)

edge/lib/ui2/activity/zones.dart only ever showed computed zones.
add a manual override: 5 bpm thresholds, one per zone's lower edge,
edited from a sheet on the zones screen (reusing OsTextField/Typed
same as the nutrition targets sheet).

trainingZones() is the one place every zone consumer already goes
through (day pipeline, live tick, workout summary, zones screen), so
the override lives there and wins outright when set, falling back to
the computed karvonen/observed/tanaka set when it's not. clearing all
five fields goes back to computed.

add siri/shortcuts intent to enable tomorrow's alarm (#392)

* add siri/shortcuts intent to enable tomorrow's alarm (#322)

only the query intents existed (recovery/strain/sleep) plus one action
intent for breathing. no write-capable one for alarms.

turns out we already had the mechanism for this - StartBreathingIntent
sets a flag in the app group and opens the app, AppState picks it up on
launch/resume and does the real thing since the widget process has no
BLE. same pattern here: EnableTomorrowAlarmIntent latches
enable_tomorrow_alarm, AppState flips tomorrow's weekday slot on via
setScheduleDay (same as tapping the toggle on the Alarm screen) and
re-arms the band if connected.

deliberately doesn't take a time param - it just turns on whatever
hour/minute tomorrow already has, so there's nothing for siri to
mis-parse and no new time to type. also sends you to the alarm screen
after so you can see it actually flipped.

pulled the weekday math into a named helper (tomorrowScheduleWeekday)
with its own test instead of eyeballing the DateTime.weekday off-by-one
inline.

* fix the two things sourcery caught on the alarm intent

1. weekday was recomputed when AppState consumed the latch, not when
   siri actually ran the intent - so a request right before midnight
   could resume after midnight and enable the wrong day. now swift
   computes "tomorrow" itself at perform() time and hands the app the
   weekday, not a bare bool.

2. the latch got cleared before setScheduleDay finished, so a
   DB/BLE hiccup silently ate the request forever. now it re-latches
   the weekday if the write throws, so it just retries next resume
   instead of vanishing.

dropped tomorrowScheduleWeekday() since dart doesn't compute the day
anymore - swift does, at the right moment.

sleep detail: link to naps, fix stale comment (#391)

* link sleep detail to naps, fix stale comment

nap editing already shipped (naps.dart, sleep_nap writer) but you could
only get to it from the health screen. added a "Naps" button next to
the sleep window buttons so it's reachable from the night you're
already looking at. also the old comment here said nap edits had no
writer, which stopped being true a few commits ago.

* naps button: move it out of the window card

sourcery caught it: _windowCard bails out (returns null) on a day with
no scored main sleep, so the naps button went with it - but naps can
happen on a day that has no main sleep too (off overnight, worn all
day, rejected night). pulled it into its own helper and render it in
both places.

* naps button: also disable while the day is still loading

coderabbit caught it - _goDay swaps _day before _load() resolves, so a
tap in that window opened naps for the day you'd just left.

fix strain/calories/zone minutes resetting to 0 after a hard-kill relaunch mid-workout (#381)

* fix: strain/calories/zone minutes no longer reset to 0 after a hard-kill relaunch mid-workout

the reconcile path rehydrated activeWorkout from the session row but always
zeroed the live tallies going forward since "can't rebuild from one DB row".
now _tickWorkout snapshots per-minute HR + zone-seconds + the calorie bpm
histogram + peak to a new live_workout_tally table every ~30s, and reconcile
restores from it instead of zeroing. offline gap (the time the app was
actually dead) is never billed as active minutes - only the finished tally
up to the last snapshot comes back. row gets deleted on stop/cancel/stale-finalize
so it can't leak onto a future session reusing the id.

* fix two things sourcery caught on the tally save

1. persist only completed minutes (_perMinute), not the dense getter that
   folds in the minute still in progress - restoring that as a full 60s
   minute let a partial pre-kill minute outweigh a real one in strain.
2. stop/cancel now await any tally save the last tick already dispatched
   before deleting the row - otherwise that save could land after the
   delete and resurrect a stale row for a future workout reusing the id.

gate the live event write behind resetgate too (#388)

onRecordsBatch/onCommitBatch/onArchiveRecord all check the reset flag before
writing, but _onLiveEvent (wristOn/battery/alarm events) never did. band
stays connected during a reset, so an event landing mid-wipe got written
straight into the fresh db. same fix as the others, plus a static assert
in reset_quiesces_ingest_test.dart so it can't regress silently again.

add smart wake window (#390)

opt-in early buzz inside a window before the alarm's set time, if the band
sees a light-sleep-ish signature (hr up a bit vs the night's own baseline,
no big movement). off by default, per weekday, capped at 45 min.

the safety bit: the window's end time IS the existing armed alarm - the
verified set_alarm mechanism nobody touches here. this only ever adds an
early run_alarm buzz. if ble is down, motion/hr is ambiguous, or nothing
ever detects light sleep, the original alarm still fires on the band's own
clock exactly like before. never later, never skipped, because nothing in
this path can change it.

piggybacks the engine's existing 30s keepalive tick instead of a new timer.

fix oura link test's real-time flake under full-suite CI (#389)

the "held reading is written once the anchor arrives" oura test failed
every full-suite CI run but passed 16/16 alone. traced it to
ingestForTest's default replyTimeout/confirmTimeout of 50ms — real
wall-clock, not a fake clock. every oura test answers its scripted
writes inside the same zero-delay spin loop so nothing should ever
actually hit that timeout, but 50ms isn't free on a shared ubuntu
runner ~1150 tests deep into one process (GC pauses, scheduler
jitter), so it fires early sometimes and the adapter gives up on the
anchor batch mid-session before the reading gets stamped.

confirmed the mechanism by shrinking the default to 1 microsecond
locally: reproduces the exact same "Expected length 1, Actual []"
failure at the exact same test. bumped the default to 2s instead —
still instant in practice since nothing on the happy path waits for
it, just real margin against CI jitter.

respect imperial units for strength weight (#386)

* respect imperial units for strength weight/volume

strength load was hardcoded to kg everywhere in live.dart and summary.dart
even though UnitsController already exists and handles this for
bodyweight/height/distance/pace. wired it into the stepper, the per-set
rows, volume totals and the 1RM estimate.

steppers now nudge by a clean 5 lb plate step in imperial instead of a
raw conversion of the 2.5kg exercise step (nobody loads a bar in 5.5 lb
increments). storage stays kg either way, only display/step changed.

a few of the affected strings are localized ARB templates that bake "kg"
into the sentence itself rather than taking it as a parameter
(activityLiveVolumeSetsSubtitle, activityLiveKgVolumeUnit,
activityLiveWeightRepsLogged, activitySummaryOneRepMax). translating a
proper lb variant into 5 languages is a bigger job than this ticket, so
imperial bypasses those templates with a plain english fallback and
metric keeps using the real translations unchanged.

* also fix the share card's strength volume — same kg bug

found while reviewing the live/summary fix: share.dart has the exact
same strength volume figure baked to kg in two spots (the stat chip and
the hero number), and it already takes a UnitsController param for
distance/pace. wired it the same way.

add lab-results csv import (#385)

* add lab-results csv import, mirroring the journal reimport path

lab_result had manual entry + export but no way to bring an edited
csv back in, unlike journal which already has this. same pattern:
header signature detection, reject-never-clamp validation, dedupe
on (marker, taken_on), falls through to the vendor importer if the
header doesn't match.

unknown marker keys are rejected rather than silently spawning a
new custom marker with no label/unit/range.

* lab csv import: keep the unit column byte-exact

sourcery caught it - validation trimmed the unit before storing it,
so " ng/mL " came back as "ng/mL". validate on a trimmed copy,
store the original. matches what the file comment already claimed.

* welcome: fix the import headline for a vendor-only outcome

coderabbit caught a real one - a whoop export with only a workouts
csv selected lands 0 days/journal/lab rows, and the headline fell
all the way through to "0 lab results written" for that case
(same bug existed before labs, just said "0 journal days written").

headline is now whichever counter is actually positive, in
days > journal > labs > workouts > skipped priority; everything
else that's also positive still shows below it. journal keeps its
own "replaced" line rather than folding into the generic list, since
that's a different fact (journal always replaces, days never does).

hr zone crossing buzz in live workouts (#384)

* add HR zone crossing buzz during live workouts

opt-in, off by default. pick a target zone in settings ("The band"
group), and the strap buzzes when live HR crosses into or out of it
mid-workout. debounced 5s so it doesn't fire on every PPG-noisy tick
right at the boundary — pure crossing/debounce logic is in
zone_alert.dart with its own tests, wiring lives in app_state's
_tickWorkout same as the idle-workout watch.

skips a null hr reading entirely rather than treating it as zone 0 —
otherwise a link blip mid-session reads as leaving the target zone and
buzzes for a connection hiccup, not a real crossing.

Fix movement-floor DST bug and coach API-key reuse across endpoint changes (#375)

* Fix movement-floor DST bug and coach API-key reuse across endpoint changes

Two independent issues surfaced while reviewing PR #374, neither caused
by that PR but found in the same pass:

- movement_floor_policy.dart: daysSinceFrozen computed the gap with
  to.difference(from).inDays on local-time DateTimes. A span crossing
  a spring-forward transition loses an hour of wall-clock duration, so
  a real 10-day gap (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-11) floored to 9. Fixed by
  diffing UTC-normalized calendar dates instead, matching the pattern
  dayLabelBefore already documents and follows for the same reason.

- coach.dart setup screen: the API key field was seeded once from
  CoachConfig and never revisited, while switching presets or editing
  the base URL changed only the endpoint. Saving then sent the old
  key to whatever origin was currently in the field — a stale cloud
  key could reach a newly-selected local/private endpoint, or vice
  versa, without the user re-entering or confirming it (CWE-200,
  flagged by CodeRabbit as Major). Added coachEndpointOrigin() in
  coach_config.dart and used it to track which origin the key field's
  contents belong to; the key is now cleared (and deleted from the
  keychain on save) whenever the base URL's origin actually changes.

Adds test/coach_endpoint_origin_test.dart; movement_floor_policy_test.dart
already encoded the correct expected values and needed no changes.

* Fix key-clear message loss and unreadable-key leak across endpoint changes

Two issues flagged on PR #375 against the origin-change key-clearing fix:

- Tapping a preset set _base.text (firing _onBaseChanged synchronously,
  which sets _msg to explain a cleared key) and then unconditionally
  reset _msg to null in the same setState, silently discarding that
  explanation. _msg is now cleared BEFORE _base.text is assigned.

- A key that exists but could not be read (CoachConfig.keyUnreadable)
  seeds the setup screen's key field empty, indistinguishable from "no
  key was ever set." _pendingKeyDelete was only ever armed when the
  field was visibly non-empty, so this case bypassed it: the stale,
  unreadable key survived an endpoint change untouched and could later
  be sent to the new endpoint (CWE-522, Major). _pendingKeyDelete is
  now armed on every endpoint change regardless of the field's visible
  contents, and the whole decision is extracted into a pure function,
  coachApiKeyToSave(), so the interaction is unit-testable without a
  widget tree.

Adds test/coach_api_key_to_save_test.dart covering all four
(readable/unreadable stored key) x (pending/not-pending) combinations
with an empty field, plus the non-empty-field case.

* whitespace-only key input bypassed pending key deletion

 don't treat whitespace-only key input as a real replacement.

CodeRabbit flagged this on PR #375 (CWE-200, Major) after the previous
fix landed: the _key controller's listener cleared _pendingKeyDelete
on raw `_key.text.isNotEmpty`, but coachApiKeyToSave trims the field
before deciding what to save. Whitespace-only input (e.g. a stray
pasted space) is non-empty by the raw check, so it cancelled the
pending deletion — then Save saw an effectively empty, non-pending
field and, for an unreadable stored key, left it untouched in the
keychain instead of deleting it. Same leak class the endpoint-change
fix was meant to close, just reachable through whitespace.

Extracted the decision into coachKeyFieldHasReplacement() in
coach_config.dart (trims before checking, so it can't drift from
coachApiKeyToSave's own trimming) and used it in place of the inline
check.

Adds test/coach_key_field_has_replacement_test.dart.

* stop tracking "replacement typed" as mutable state, derive it at Save

CodeRabbit found a gap in the EDGE-13 fix on PR #375: the _key listener
cleared _pendingKeyDelete as soon as any non-whitespace text appeared,
but never restored it. Typing a replacement key after an endpoint
change and then erasing it again left the flag cleared with nothing to
show for it — an unreadable stored key from the old endpoint then
survived _save() untouched and could reach the new endpoint on a later
load (CWE-200).

Rather than patch the listener again, removed it. coachApiKeyToSave
already derives "is there a real replacement" correctly by checking
_key.text.trim() at the moment Save actually runs, so tracking it
separately as mutable state was both redundant and the source of two
bugs in a row (this one and EDGE-13's whitespace case). _pendingKeyDelete
now only ever means "the endpoint changed since the stored key was
last confirmed to belong to it" — set by _onBaseChanged, cleared after
a successful save, untouched by typing.

Removes the now-unused coachKeyFieldHasReplacement() and its test.
Adds a regression case to coach_api_key_to_save_test.dart: a
replacement typed after an endpoint change and then erased (to blank
or whitespace) is still force-deleted at Save time.

* bump kAlgoVersion for daysSinceFrozen DST fix

Live HR/IMU stream ownership reconciler (#287) (#334)

* feat(ble): live HR/IMU stream ownership reconciler (#287)

A foreground connection was an implicit request for both the realtime-HR
stream (opcode 3) and the 100 Hz IMU stream (gen5 opcode 106); the
enable / HR-only / disable methods flipped the engine's live flags before
their writes went out, with nothing serialising them. A breathing close
started an OFF unawaited, a workout starting inside that window saw
"already enabled" and skipped its ON, and the older OFF then left the
workout without a stream; a feature that started while another had
streams on recorded no ownership, so when both left nothing recomputed
the remaining owner set (stopWorkout never disabled at all) and the
keep-alive kept re-arming a flood nobody read.

Every consumer is now an explicit owner (LiveStreamOwners) that the
engine reads through a provider inside one serialised, coalescing
reconciler — the only writer of opcode 3 and the high-rate bundle.
Desired and applied state are separate; applied moves only after a
successful write on a link that is still the live one (generation +
identity + a synchronous `closing` flag checked after every write and
delay); a failed write marks its bit dirty so the newest direction is
replayed before convergence; a nudge during a failed write is honoured
in the same pass, which is how disconnect()'s shutdown intent gets
through. The keep-alive re-arm and the marginal-radio fallback go through
the same pass, gated on applied state. Link priority rises as soon as
IMU is desired and holds until the OFF has landed.

gen5 policy per #287: an ordinary foreground connection owns nothing;
a mounted live-HR view, any workout, a breathing session/window and iOS
background own HR; a FOREGROUND gait workout, a bounded movement-sampling
window (no scheduler yet) and the passive strap-step opt-in (off) own
IMU. Optical opcodes 107/108 are never written on gen5. gen4 keeps its
previous behaviour through an explicit foreground-bundle owner, and its
byte sequences are unchanged, including the fresh-link defensive OFF
tail (R10/R11 OFF persists across reconnects on the strap).

AppState only mutates owners and nudges; the settle/downgrade patch and
the breathing "did I enable it" flag are gone. The resting-HR live card
host and the band device page retain an HR view while mounted.

Tests: the owner→intent table and single-step reconciler (pure), every
scenario in the #287 acceptance list through the fake-link seam
(delayed/failing/stale writes, disconnect mid-transition, link
replacement mid-bundle, keep-alive reassert, priority ordering, gen4
sequences), the AppState owner set, and both live-HR view hosts.

* fix: 60ms gap after hr write in imu-off hrHead path

reconciler's ops-list only gapped after later writes, missed the
hrHead toggleRealtimeHr itself. old enableHrOnlyLive loop always
gapped after every write, this brings it back in line.

Improve AI coach reliability: configurable timeouts, Keychain recovery, and in-flight request survival (#374)

* Improve AI coach reliability: configurable timeouts, Keychain recovery, and in-flight request survival

Three reliability issues in the AI coach:

- Requests silently died if the chat screen was left before they
  finished. CoachEngine now defers closing its shared HTTP client
  until an in-flight send() completes (requestDispose()), instead of
  aborting the request out from under it when the screen disposes.

- Saving a key could fail if a stale Keychain item from a prior
  install collided with the write (errSecDuplicateItem). CoachConfig
  now detects that specific error, deletes the stale item, and
  retries the write once.

- The provider request timeout was a hardcoded 120s, too short for a
  local model's first response (Ollama/LM Studio can take minutes to
  load a model into memory). The timeout is now user-configurable,
  but only for a local endpoint (default 5 min) — a cloud endpoint
  always uses a fixed 2-minute timeout regardless of that setting,
  since a real cloud failure surfaces in seconds, not minutes.

Adds/extends tests: coach_engine_dispose_test.dart,
coach_config_timeout_test.dart, coach_request_timeout_test.dart, and
coach_config_key_test.dart.

* Fix PR review findings: shared local-endpoint check, concurrent-send race

Two issues flagged in PR #374 review:

- The setup screen's local-endpoint check (_isLocal) only recognized
  loopback hosts, while CoachConfig.isLocalEndpoint also treats
  10.0.2.2, private IPv4 ranges, and .local hostnames as local. A
  LAN-hosted Ollama/LM Studio (e.g. a phone reaching a desktop over
  192.168.x.x) had its timeout field hidden and was silently capped
  at the fixed cloud timeout. Extracted the classification into a
  shared isLocalCoachHost(url) function that both now call.

- CoachEngine tracked in-flight requests with a single bool
  (_sending). Two overlapping send() calls could have the first one
  to finish flip it false and let a pending requestDispose() close
  the shared HTTP client while the second request was still in
  flight. Changed _sending to a counter that only allows the
  deferred dispose once it reaches zero.

Adds a regression test for the concurrent-send case in
coach_engine_dispose_test.dart; existing coach_local_endpoint_test.dart
already covers the shared host classifier.

* fix: clear stored api key when the coach endpoint changes

switching presets or editing the base url used to leave the old key sitting
in the field and in the keychain, so save carried it over to a different
origin unless you happened to notice and clear it yourself. now changing the
origin clears the visible field and force-deletes the stored key on save,
even when the key couldn't be read back (still counts as stored).

fix: hold the beat axis non-decreasing (sleep staging threw on 6 of 8 days), bump kAlgoVersion to 88; quiesce ingest during a data reset (#365)

* fix: hold the beat axis non-decreasing, bump kAlgoVersion to 88

`beat_ts_ms` is a modelled beat position: `beatTimesMs` anchors on the
record's sub-second stamp under the model that the record's LAST beat sits
at that stamp, then walks the intervals backwards from it. When two adjacent
records' anchors sit closer together than one beat, the model places record
N+1's beat 0 EARLIER than record N's last beat, and beats are emitted in
record order — so the axis steps backwards.

Measured on a live install, over one day's derive window:
39,066 beats, 94 inversions, every one at beat_index = 0, by 7-672 ms.

analytics' `cardioStager` binary-searches that axis and asserts it ascends.
One inverted pair took a whole night's staging down:

  derive day 2026-09-08 FAILED/skipped: Bad state: sleep-staging isolate
  failed: 'rrTsMs must be non-decreasing — the beat window is binary-searched'

Six of eight days in the pending span threw on every pass; the newest day
that survived was the previous night, so the app sat on "Crunching last
night's numbers" and pressing Sync again looked like the only lever. The
BLE offload was healthy throughout — it reached the live edge every time.

The assert is compiled out in RELEASE, so shipped builds never threw. They
mis-selected each 300 s window's beats instead and banked the result, which
is the worse failure of the two and is why kAlgoVersion moves: affected days
are otherwise served from cache (`finalizedDayIds` / `sleepSessionCandidate`
both key on it) and can never be told apart from good ones after the fact.

THE ORDER IS NOT WHAT IS WRONG. Beats arrive in the order the strap detected
them and that order is the rhythm — beat_clock_read_path_test pins it. So
`monotonizeBeatAxis` repairs only the modelled placement, holding each beat
no earlier than the one before it. A sort would reshuffle a true interval
series to satisfy an assert. Interval values and their order are untouched;
a held beat lands on a zero-length gap, which the axis already contains (the
`rr_ts_ms` staircase ties a whole record's beats to one millisecond) and
which analytics' window gather is written for.

Called on both paths into `Substrate.rrTsMs`: at the end of
`decodeSubstrate`, and at the page seam in `buildSubstrate()` — a seam is
invisible to either page loader, since each places its own beats correctly
and then appends.

Also, "Synced through 11:06" on Home
------------------------------------
The data edge was only readable from Profile > Devices, so there was no way
to see how far a sync had actually got. It reads the band's own clock on the
newest record BANKED, not last contact: a connection that transfers nothing
is not progress and must not render as progress. "Today" is the day the
screen is already showing rather than `DateTime.now()`, so it cannot
contradict the date line above it after midnight, and it renders on the
loading/failed/first-run path too — which is when the question is loudest.

Two fixes fall out of putting that value on screen:
  - `_onRecord` advanced `_lastRecTs` BEFORE awaiting the insert, and the
    field only moves forward, so a failed write advertised a record the
    database does not hold for the rest of the process.
  - `resetAllData()` wiped the database but left `_lastRecTs` set, so a
    re-pair without a relaunch showed the deleted install's timestamp.

kAnalyticsPin/kProtocolPin are UNCHANGED — the repair is entirely edge-side.

* fix: refuse record ingest while "delete everything" is running

Review of #365 caught that clearing `_lastRecTs` in `resetAllData()` can be
undone by the band it is deleting.

`resetAllData()` wipes the database but leaves the strap CONNECTED: its own
documented order puts `signOut` — and the `unpair` inside it — LAST, because
that flips the route and unwinds the UI. So the band keeps handing over
historical records straight across the wipe, and one that lands after it is
written into the fresh database and re-advertised as the data edge: the
deleted installation, visible again on Home, with nothing left to explain it.

There are TWO ingest paths and the wider one bypasses AppState entirely:

  onRecord:        _onRecord                      // singles
  onRecordsBatch:  LocalDb.insertRecordsBatch     // the drain, straight to db

The drain carries the volume, so guarding only `_onRecord` would have looked
like a fix while leaving the real hole open. Both now refuse while `_resetting`
is up.

A refusal flag rather than a reordering: tearing the link down first is a
change to the CONNECTION LIFECYCLE, not to the wipe, and that ordering is
deliberate and load-bearing. Nothing is lost by refusing — none of these
records have been ACKed, so they are still on the band. The flag is raised
before the wipe and lowered in a `finally`: a half-reset install that silently
drops every record would be worse than the race it closes.

Also read `insertRecord`'s result before advancing the data edge. It returns
`Future<bool>`, and today can only return true or throw — the false path is not
reachable — but the ordering fix is about not claiming data we do not hold, and
ignoring the one value that says whether we hold it made that promise on trust.

`test/reset_quiesces_ingest_test.dart` greps rather than runs: `_resetting` is
private and `resetAllData` needs the whole plugin stack, while the failure mode
is a THIRD ingest path added later that forgets the guard — invisible to any
test that runs the code. Same approach as link_priority_structural_test.dart.
It pins both guards, the raise-before-wipe ordering, the finally, and that
`insertRecordsBatch` is never handed over as a bare tear-off again.

* fix: quiesce the headless drain too while "delete everything" runs

The reset guard added in dd124aa covers AppState's own ingest callbacks. It
cannot cover the OTHER engine: `runHeadlessSync` (background_sync.dart) builds
a second BleEngine whose sinks go straight to LocalDb with no AppState anywhere
in scope. A drain already in flight when the user confirms the reset therefore
kept writing into the freshly wiped database — the deleted installation, back
again. Half a quiesce is a worse thing to ship than none.

Narrow, and worth closing anyway. A foreground engine PREEMPTS a background
drainer when it connects (`BleEngine._claimBand`) and AppState connects on
launch, so the window needs a drain the foreground never preempted. And the
only thing standing between a reset and a FRESH headless drain today is an
accident: `prefs.clear()` makes `PairedDevice.load()` return null, so the next
run bails. Nobody wrote that as a safeguard, and it stops working silently the
day the paired device is cached anywhere else.

`ResetGate` replaces the private `_resetting` field so both engines read one
flag. A static is the right mechanism ONLY because there is no second isolate
to hide from it: every headless entry point runs in the MAIN isolate (Android
pre-warms the FlutterEngine and runs `main()` with no Activity; the two iOS
wakes are main-isolate), and the WorkManager tasks that did have their own
isolate were pulled for exactly that class of problem — `main()` still cancels
them by unique name on every Android start and nothing registers a
`callbackDispatcher`. `HeadlessSyncGate` already rests on the same assumption.
reset_gate.dart says so, and says that reintroducing a background isolate
breaks this silently.

THE COMMIT SINK THROWS RATHER THAN RETURNING QUIETLY, in both engines. Only
`onCommit` banks raws + archives + trim cursor in one transaction, and
`DrainController` reads durability FROM A THROW — its safe-trim invariant even
forbids `onRecordsBatch` without it, to close "the latent hole where
archive-only chunks would ACK and trim flash that was never stored". A silent
return there would tell the drain the chunk was banked; it would ACK, and the
band would trim flash this reset refused to store. That turns a race into real
data loss, on a band whose records are the only surviving copy if the reset
then fails. A throw blocks the ACK and the records stay on the strap. The
non-ACK sinks (onRecord / onRecordsBatch / onEvent / onArchiveRecord) return
quietly, which is safe precisely because none of them gate the trim.

The structural test grows to cover the second engine: every write sink consults
the gate, no sink is handed over as a bare LocalDb tear-off again, the headless
bail sits ahead of `PairedDevice.load()`, and both commit sinks throw. It greps
rather than runs for the same reason as before — the failure mode is a sink
added later that forgets the guard, which no test that exercises the code sees.

* fix: count resets in ResetGate so an overlapping one cannot reopen the window

`resetAllData()` is awaited but does not block the UI: the confirm dialog is
already dismissed when it starts, `backToRoot` only runs when it returns, and
wiping a real database takes seconds. So a user can walk back into Settings and
confirm a second wipe on top of the first.

With a bare bool the first to finish lowered the flag while the second was
still wiping — reopening the exact window this class exists to close, at the
worst possible moment. Counted, the gate stays shut until the last reset leaves.

`leave()` clamps at zero rather than going negative. An unbalanced leave is a
bug either way, but one that drove the count below zero would make the NEXT
reset's `enter()` fail to open the gate at all, and that is the failure that
loses data. Absorb it instead.

Found by review on #365.

fix(chord): keep tracked paths correct across structural mutation

A wrapper baked its path at creation, so a reference held across a
structural mutation kept addressing its old index: unshift then a write
through a held element edited its neighbour, and a write after a splice
could produce a path the replica cannot resolve. The baseline diff this
tracker replaced was immune, because its dirty paths were only hints and
the ops came from comparing values.

A wrapper now holds a cell (parent link plus segment) and the path is
walked at use time, so renumbering an element corrects every descendant.
pop/shift/unshift/splice and length truncation shift live children by the
delta and mark removed ones dead; sort/reverse/fill/copyWithin relocate
them by identity. Renumbering iterates a set of live cells rather than the
lookup cache, which is keyed by index and can evict a child that is still
held. Writes through an element that left the document mutate it and
record nothing, as plain JS and the baseline diff both do.

One object can occupy several positions in the tree. A wrapper is now
shared per target and holds a cell per position, and a write emits an op
for each, which is what the baseline diff produced for the same shape.
Positions are registered when a path is read, when a tracked value is
assigned elsewhere, and when one is inserted by an array mutator (only the
inserted range is examined; scanning the array made every structural
mutation O(n)). A blocked view of an object gets its own wrapper so the
reserved-key guard cannot be bypassed through a safe alias.

Paths are cached per cell against a counter that only structural mutation
bumps, and the per-write cell walk is skipped until a document actually
aliases something.

`assertTargetSmokeHealth` checked the API and the gateway and called that the
release SHA. The release gate's three Playwright shards drive a third surface,

The surfaces do not share a clock. API and gateway roll on ECS; the frontend is
a Vercel deployment `deploy-staging.yml` aliases onto the host, and Vercel swaps
the alias only once the build reaches READY.

Measured on the v0.13.25 gate (run 35392201088, PR #7422,
RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA=8a1e38dc97ba76ae2aba7fe9c7cce284fa05af23):

  20:32:06Z  deploy-staging 35391030403 "Deploy staging web to Vercel" starts
  20:32:38Z  Vercel dpl_ZWu71zWXoWKvwGBr9uCs17FVu7Ha (sha 8a1e38dc) created
  20:36:16Z  release-gate browser shards 1-3 start
  20:50Z     that deployment still INITIALIZING; alias still on dpl_43b4...
             (sha fa68c114, built 05:22Z)

So the shards drove a frontend 15 hours behind the release while api and gateway
both reported it. Verified live with the bypass: staging.kortix.com/api/health
returns commit fa68c114d7a9fcffc34f40497f2980f392797a47.

Changes:

- deployment-bypass.ts gains deploymentBypassRequestHeaders(): the bypass header

The webUrl host pin already existed in resolveTargetSmokeConfig, so no new
validation was needed there.

No deploy ordering change, no wait/retry loop, no shard-matrix change. The gate

fix(connectors): adding a tool authorizes the project account, not the clicker's (#7423)

* fix(connectors): adding a tool authorizes the project account, not the clicker's

`useToolConnect` — the onboarding "connect this tool" flow — documented itself
as authorizing "the PROJECT's shared account", then sent no `owner` on either
verb. Both connector-scoped routes default an absent owner to `me`
(`apps/api/src/projects/lib/connection-access.ts:94`, applied at
`apps/api/src/connectors/db-deps.ts:2325` and `:2439`), so the flow ran
`ensureMemberConnection` and landed `owner_type = 'member'`,
`owner_id = <whoever clicked>`, labelled "Private connection".

A `member` row is reachable only by that one user and NEVER by a service
account (`connectionIsReachable`, `connection-access.ts:42`). So the
project-owned row that connector creation had already made stayed
unauthorized forever, every other member got nothing, and every trigger got
nothing — while the UI reported the tool connected.

Verified against the live local stack (real Supabase JWT, real Composio, DB
read-back of `kortix.connector_connections`):

  body {}                  -> owner_type=member owner_id=<caller>  "Private connection"
  body {"owner":"project"} -> owner_type=project owner_id=null     (shared row reused)
  body {"owner":"nonsense"}-> 400 owner must be "me" or "project"

Replace `requestToolAuthorization` with `toolConnectSteps`, a `start`/`finalize`
pair that names `owner: 'project'` on BOTH verbs and pins finalize to the
connection id the start returned. The owner has to match across the two:
finalize selects the row by owner scope, so finalizing a `project`
authorization without the owner polls the caller's own member connection and
never reports the shared account active. Same shape and same reasoning as
`projectConnectSteps` in `use-pipedream-connect-project.ts`.

No SDK change: `connectorConnect` and `connectorFinalize` already take
`{ owner, connectionId }` and their pass-through is already tested
(`connectors.test.ts:1168-1194`). The host was calling them wrong. This also
moves off the deprecated `pipedream*` aliases to the canonical names; both
stay exported, so nothing published breaks.

The previous unit test was titled "always authorizes the project shared
account" but its stub ignored the options argument, so it passed while the
real call sent nothing. The replacement asserts the exact options both verbs
receive.

* fix(connectors): name the project owner in usePipedreamConnect too

`usePipedreamConnect` documents itself as connecting "the project's shared
account" and sent no `owner` on either verb — the same defect just fixed in
`use-tool-connect.ts`, with the same consequence: the connector-scoped routes
default an absent owner to `me`
(`apps/api/src/projects/lib/connection-access.ts:94`, applied at
`apps/api/src/connectors/db-deps.ts:2325` and `:2439`), so it would authorize
the caller's own private account.

This hook has no callers today — every live surface uses
`usePipedreamConnectProject` / `usePipedreamConnectMember`, both of which name
their owner correctly. It is left in place rather than deleted because it was
deliberately split out of `connectors-view.tsx` for bundle reasons documented
in `connectors-page.chunk.test.ts:17-21`; that decision is not this PR's to
reverse. Naming the owner means wiring it up cannot reintroduce the bug.

Extracts `appConnectSteps` so the owner on both verbs is asserted without a
renderer, matching `toolConnectSteps` and `projectConnectSteps`.

perf(web): batch the entrypoint bundle rewrite into one sed pass (#7421)

The frontend entrypoint rewrote baked NEXT_PUBLIC_ values with one sed
process per file. /app/apps/web/.next holds 2141 .js/.html files, so every
container start spawned 2141 sed processes before `exec node
apps/web/server.js`.

Measured in kortix/kortix-frontend:dev-ec6cbdb7 (linux/amd64 under
emulation on an arm64 host):

  before: rewrite 39.8s, first HTTP 200 at 54s
  after:  rewrite  2.5s, first HTTP 200 at 17s

The absolute numbers are inflated by emulation. The ratio is process-spawn
overhead and is real on native Fargate, where prod web tasks run at 512 CPU
units. The cost is paid on every deploy, scale-out, and crash replacement.

Changes:
- `find | while read; sed -i` -> `find -print0 | xargs -0 -r sed -i`.
- Group the find predicates: `\( -name '*.js' -o -name '*.html' \)`.
  Without the parens, `-print0` binds only to the `*.html` branch, so find
  emits 2 paths instead of 2141 and every .js chunk keeps its build-time
  placeholder. The old implicit `-print` hid this; `-print0` makes it fatal.
- Log the rewrite duration so the cost stays visible in ECS task logs.

Rewritten bundles are byte-identical: md5 over all 2141 files is
69b02e55ec5d3e1b16861db93393c1f0 in both the before and after containers.

`xargs -0 -r` verified against the image base, Debian 12 bookworm
(node:22-slim), GNU findutils 4.9.0. Script syntax verified with the image's
own /bin/sh (dash).

apps/web/docker-entrypoint.test.mjs extracts the live pipeline from the
shipped script and asserts .js/.html get rewritten, .txt/.css decoys do not,
and the un-parenthesized find leaves every .js file untouched.

fix(infra): own the ECS stabilize budget and report why a rollout failed (#7420)

* fix(infra): own the ECS stabilize budget and report why a rollout failed

`aws ecs wait services-stable` has a vendor-fixed budget of 40 attempts x 15s
= 600s and, on expiry, prints only "Max attempts exceeded".

Two defects, both in infra/scripts/ecs-deploy.sh, which rolls dev, staging,
prod and rollback-prod:

1. The budget was marginal. Run 35388160843 / job 105741051220 (main
   ec6cbdb793) failed the dev frontend roll after 9m57s on that 600s cap,
   while the last successful roll (run 35382033823) took 7m53s — ~2 minutes
   of headroom no caller could raise.
2. A timeout reported nothing. "Max attempts exceeded" cannot distinguish a
   slow roll from a crash-looping task, so a human cannot tell whether the
   built image is safe to promote. That blocked a production promote decision.

Replaces the waiter with a self-implemented poll over `describe-services`:

- ECS_STABILIZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 900) is the whole budget, declared
  once; ECS_STABILIZE_POLL_SECONDS (default 15) is the interval.
- rolloutState == FAILED exits immediately instead of burning the budget.
- A timeout or failure prints, before exiting non-zero: every deployment's
  status/rolloutState/rolloutStateReason and counts, the last 10 service
  events with timestamps, capped stopped-task stoppedReason plus each
  container's exitCode/reason, and the awslogs group as a copy-pasteable
  `aws logs tail`. Every diagnostic call soft-fails so it cannot mask the
  rollout verdict.

Deploy ordering, image tags, task sizing and the Terraform cpu/memory
propagation are untouched.

No real ECS rollout was exercised: this environment has no AWS credentials.

* fix(infra): report rollout observations, never conclude a cause

Review catch: `print_stopped_task_diagnostics` printed

    stopped tasks: none — the roll is slow, not crash-looping

which is false whenever a rollout is wedged with tasks still in PENDING — an
image pull, exhausted capacity or subnet IPs, or an ELB health check below its
threshold. In all of those nothing reaches STOPPED inside the window, so the
line told the on-call the opposite of what was happening. It also broke this
change's own rule: hand back evidence, not a verdict.

- The no-stopped-tasks branch now states only the observation, says plainly
  that it does NOT mean the roll is merely slow, names the PENDING causes, and
  points at the counts, live-task breakdown and events.
- Adds `print_live_task_diagnostics`: the lastStatus breakdown of tasks whose
  DESIRED status is RUNNING, plus any container `reason`. That is the signal
  which actually discriminates the PENDING wedge, and it names the cause
  (e.g. CannotPullContainerError) outright. Two capped, soft-failing calls on
  the failure path only; a container with no reason contributes no line.
- The FAILED headline now carries running/desired/pending, so the counts lead
  both failure paths.

Two more unsupported claims found by auditing every diagnostic line:

- The `only evidence that separates slow from crash-looping` comment made the
  same overclaim; rewritten.
- The awslogs hint printed `stream=<none>/<container>/<task-id>` when the
  task-def declares no `awslogs-stream-prefix` — a stream path that cannot
  exist, since the driver then names the stream after the container id. It now
  prints the prefixed form only when a prefix exists.

Also corrects the header comment's 7m53s to the ~7m23s waiter figure, matching
the measurement correction already made in the PR body.

Nothing else concluded a cause the data does not support.

Test: a fifth case asserts the new wording, asserts the old sentence is
absent, and asserts the PENDING breakdown still names the real cause, so a
regression to the verdict-style line fails.

Validate the OpenCode session pin on read; document both CodeQL sinks (#7426)

Assessment of two open CodeQL dataflow alerts on `main`. Neither is
exploitable. One gets a real control anyway; both get a comment at the sink
so the next reader does not re-litigate them.

Alert 6375 — js/file-access-to-http, control.ts:373
Flow: boot.ts:3117 readFileSync(OPENCODE_SESSION_PIN_PATH) -> control.ts:365
sessionId -> control.ts:371 url -> control.ts:373 fetch(url).
Not exploitable: the destination is lifecycle.ts:2646
`http://127.0.0.1:${livePort()}`. Scheme, host and port are literal, and the
port is the daemon's own. The id is encodeURIComponent-escaped into one path
segment. The only file data on the wire is the session id, sent to loopback.

Hardening: the pin file lives under the `kortix` home and the agent's own
shell tools run as that uid, so its bytes are not guaranteed to come from a
validating writer. The write side already enforced
/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/; the read side trusted the file. Read, write and
validation now all live in runtime-state.ts, and `readOpenCodeSessionPin`
rejects a malformed pin as "no session pinned" — a state every caller already
handles by creating a fresh session. `readPinnedOpencodeSessionId` keeps its
name and delegates.

Alert 6571 — js/http-to-file-access, pi/runtime.ts:906
Flow: relay.ts:29-34 fetch(/turn-stream) -> relay.ts:69 res.json() ->
relay.ts:71 type guard -> relay.ts:72 claimedInitialTurn.prompt ->
pi/boot.ts:98 -> pi/boot.ts:180 runtime.admit({text: claim.prompt}) ->
transcript -> runtime.ts:902 dump.transcript -> runtime.ts:906 writeFileSync.
Not exploitable: the flagged argument (columns 26-46) is
`JSON.stringify(dump)` — the content, not the path. dumpPath() derives from
`cfg.piStateDir` and `sessionId`, both process env, and POST /kortix/env
cannot set either (project-env.ts:34-44 skips every KORTIX_-prefixed key; the
control.ts allowlist holds 7 names, neither of them). No response can
redirect the write. The dump is read back with JSON.parse behind a
version + rootId check and consumed as transcript data, never executed.
Dir 0o700, file 0o600, and piStateDir sits outside /workspace.

No code change for 6571 — the path is already env-derived and contained.

Tests: 8 new cases in src/__tests__/runtime-state.test.ts cover the read
guard with ../../etc/passwd, /etc/passwd, a newline-injected pin, an
over-long id, and legitimate ids. Removing the guard fails 3 of them.

fix(api): report a wrong prompt-attachment part index as 404, not 409 (#7424)

`resolvePromptAttachments` checked the command's status before it checked the
handle. A wrong `part_index` therefore answered 409
`attachment_command_not_running` whenever the command had left `running`, and
404 `attachment_not_found` while it was still running. The same wrong index got
two different answers on timing alone, and the 409 told the caller to retry an
error no retry can fix.

The payload that decides whether a part index is valid is on the same joined
row as the status, so the status is not needed to answer. Check the handle
first. A handle that names no real file part of the command reports 404
whatever the command is doing. A handle that would resolve keeps the transient
409, so a caller can still tell "wrong index" from "wrong time".

SESS-30 asserts the 404 at
tests/src/flows/session-attachments.flow.ts:145-148 and saw both answers.

Verified over real HTTP against the local test-profile API, all four cases:
  running     + index 1 (valid) -> 200
  running     + index 0 (wrong) -> 404 attachment_not_found
  not running + index 1 (valid) -> 409 attachment_command_not_running
  not running + index 0 (wrong) -> 404 attachment_not_found  (was 409)

The new integration case pins the guard ORDER, not just the two guards, and
asserts the `code` so the two conditions stay distinguishable.

fix(connectors): revive the shared Connect CTAs for a connector's sole account

Both shared "Connect" CTAs in the connector detail modal were dead for any
connector with exactly one shared account — the state right after the connector
is created, because sync auto-creates that one project-owned row.

`usePipedreamConnectProject` called the CONNECTION-scoped connect route. For the
connector's EFFECTIVE project default — pinned, OR the sole active project-owned
row even when unpinned — `apps/api/src/projects/routes/r4.ts` answers 409 and
names the connector-scoped route to use instead (INVARIANT, 2026-09-16
`account_required` rule). Since 6b7e3c27c5 those auto-created rows are no longer
pinned, so the sole row is that effective default and the button 409'd.

The hook now does what the 409 asks: it falls back to the connector-scoped
connect with `owner: 'project'`. The fix is in the hook, so all four call sites
are covered at once — the modal's `connect` and `replace` CTAs, the in-session
connector gate, and the Accounts-tab "Add".

Two traps the fallback had to avoid:

- Only the default account is redirected. Several project-owned connections per
  connector are supported and distinguished by label; `owner: 'project'` reuses
  `ensureDefaultConnection`, so redirecting a labelled NON-default account would
  re-authorize the default and leave the new row unauthorized. The 409 itself is
  the discriminator, so the server stays the only authority on "effective
  default" and the client never replicates that rule.
- The finalize must match the connect. One handler serves both the
  connection-scoped `connect` and `connect/finalize` (r4.ts builds them in one
  loop), so the 409 blocks finalize too. And the connector-scoped finalize
  defaulted an absent `owner` to `me`, which polls the caller's member account
  and never reports the shared one active — a silent 10-minute timeout.

`connectorFinalize` therefore gains an optional `{ owner, connectionId }`.
Additive: one new exported type, no rename, no removal.

The 409 status alone identifies the guard (it is the only 409 that handler
returns), and it is read structurally rather than via `instanceof ApiError`,
which can be false across the SDK's ESM build and IIFE global.

`kortix tui` downloads its binary from the release the `kortix` binary came

Both `build-cli` jobs gain a second cross-compile loop over the same four

Each TUI asset also gets a `.sha256` beside it. The launcher verifies the

`src/tui-bin.ts` is the managed-binary resolver, modeled on `opencode-bin.ts`:

  1. KORTIX_TUI_BIN               explicit path, used as-is
  2. ~/.kortix/tui/<version>/kortix-tui   the cache for THIS CLI's version
  3. <base>/<tag>/kortix-tui-<os>-<arch>  downloaded, checksum-verified

`<base>` is https://github.com/kortix-ai/suna/releases/download (the scheme
scripts/install.sh already uses), `<tag>` is `v<version>` for a release and
`dev-latest` for a `X.Y.Z-dev.<sha8>` build — the only tag deploy-dev.yml ever
puts those assets on. KORTIX_TUI_RELEASE_BASE re-points it for tests.

The version is validated with the same strictness as `isValidOpencodeVersion`,
and for the same reason: it is spliced into a URL AND into a path under
~/.kortix, so `../x` or a newline would redirect the download or escape the
cache. `dev` fails that check on purpose — a source build has no release to
match, so the command says `pnpm --filter @kortix/tui bundle` instead of
inventing a URL. It still READS ~/.kortix/tui/dev/kortix-tui, so a locally
built binary dropped there works with no env var.

Every download is checked against the release's `.sha256` asset before the file
becomes executable; the checksum is required, not optional. A mismatch leaves
nothing behind — not the binary, not the staging file — because the alternative
is an 80 MB tampered or half-written executable that every later run would exec
without asking again. The verified bytes are staged beside the destination and
renamed into place, so a concurrent `kortix tui` never sees a partial file.

`src/commands/tui.ts` is now a launcher. It validates `--host` (still the CLI's
message: `kortix hosts login <name>`), resolves the binary, and
`spawn(bin, [], { stdio: 'inherit' })` so the child owns the real tty — raw
mode, the alternate screen, resize. SIGINT/SIGTERM are ignored while the child
runs: Ctrl+C reaches the whole foreground group, and the launcher dying first
would return the shell prompt while the TUI still holds the alternate screen.
The command exits with the child's code (128+signo on a signal death).

`--host` / `--project` / `--session` reach the child as KORTIX_TUI_HOST /
KORTIX_PROJECT_ID / KORTIX_SESSION_ID. KORTIX_TUI_HOST is new in
apps/tui/src/auth/hosts.ts and outranks the env token: `--host` is an explicit
claim about WHICH instance, and a stale KORTIX_TOKEN exported in a shell would
otherwise silently win and the flag would do nothing. A name that is gone falls
through to the normal order rather than dead-ending.

First run on a tty asks `Install now? [Y/n]`. Off a tty it never starts an
80 MB download on someone's behalf: exit 2 and `kortix tui --install`.
`--install` installs without asking and does not take the terminal;
`--uninstall` removes ~/.kortix/tui. `kortix uninstall` already took the whole
of ~/.kortix, which is where the managed opencode lives too.

feat(cli): kortix tui (experimental)

`kortix tui [--host <name>] [--project <id>] [--session <id>]` opens the
Kortix terminal client from the installed binary. No clone, no pnpm, no env
gate.

Auth is resolved exactly like every other subcommand — `--host` goes through
`loadAuthForHost`, otherwise `loadAuth()`, which already yields the synthetic
`sandbox` host when `KORTIX_TOKEN` is set — and the resulting `Auth` becomes
the TUI's `ResolvedHost` (`/v1` mount via `sdkBackendUrl`, the host's
`default_project`, and `source: 'env'` so a rejected `KORTIX_TOKEN` can be
named). A `--host` that is not logged in is an error; no host at all is not,
because the TUI owns a login screen and the user asked for the app.

The renderer is reached through a dynamic import, so no other subcommand loads
React or dlopen's OpenTUI's 5.5 MB native library. `kortix --help` lists it
with the same `Experimental:` blurb prefix `apps` uses, `kortix tui --help`
prints the usage, the key summary and the docs URL, and one stderr line names
it experimental before the alternate screen takes over — the only thing that
survives in scrollback afterwards.

Two things had to change to make the binary carry it:

  - `@opentui/core` declares its prebuilt native libraries as os/cpu-gated
    optionalDependencies, so pnpm installs only the current machine's. Bun
    inlines process.platform/arch per --compile target and keeps exactly the
    matching `await import("@opentui/core-<os>-<arch>")`, which then has to
    resolve at BUILD time. All six are direct dependencies of @kortix/tui now
    (both libc variants for Linux, since OPENTUI_LIBC is read at runtime), so
    all four release targets cross-compile from one runner as they always did.
  - apps/cli/tsconfig.json learns OpenTUI's JSX factory, so `tsc --noEmit`
    type-checks across the boundary instead of stopping at TS6142. A breaking
    change to `runTui`'s signature now fails the CLI's own typecheck.

The command exits the process itself rather than returning to the CLI's usual
`process.exitCode` drain: measured on the compiled binary against a real host,
the app's live queries keep Bun's event loop alive after `renderer.destroy()`

fix(sessions): stop the sidebar reordering itself under the user (#7384)

* fix(sessions): stop the sidebar reordering itself under the user

Sub-sessions visibly swapped places in the project sidebar roughly once a
minute. Two causes, both in the sort key.

**The key was bookkeeping.** `sessionLastActivityAt` falls back to
`project_sessions.updated_at` for a session with no activity record, and that
column is advanced with no turn behind it by the 60s sandbox heartbeat, the
reaper, stuck-session reconcile, runtime-identity recovery, branch GC telemetry
and the trigger access sweep. Paired with the sidebar's own 60s refetch, the
list re-sorted against freshly-bumped timestamps at exactly the observed
cadence.

That fallback is not the bug — its comment is. It says step 3 "retires itself:
any such session gets an exact stamp on its next prompt", and for a prompt a
BROWSER sends that is true: the preview proxy calls `recordSessionActivity`
after its dedupe claim. It was the only caller in the repo. A prompt the
PLATFORM delivers — a coordinator spawning a sub-session, a trigger, a channel
message, an approval resume — runs through the lifecycle engine, which never
touches the proxy, so those sessions never got a stamp and rode `updated_at`
forever. They are precisely the sessions nested in the sidebar.

So the engine stamps too, on `delivered` only, best-effort and never awaited —
the same contract the proxy uses, because a failed stamp must degrade ordering
and never the prompt. The existing fallback is left exactly as it is; it now
retires itself the way it always claimed to.

**And ties were not broken.** `directSubsessions` sorts on `updated_at ?? 0`,
so every child missing a timestamp tied at 0 and kept ARRIVAL order — whatever
order the sandbox listing came back in. That order is re-derived on each
refetch and the snapshot writer persists a pure reorder as a change, so the
churn reached every client. Ids are stable and unique; they are the tiebreak.

Verified: web sidebar + session-label suites 570 pass / 0 fail, API typecheck

fix(session): an idle session's Files panel shows its files, not a forever spinner (#7367)

* fix(session): an idle session's Files panel shows its files, not a forever spinner

A parked sandbox refuses every read by design: `shouldAutoResumeStoppedSandbox`
rejects GET on a session-data port, so the proxy answers `503 sandbox_not_ready`
from the session row without dialling the box. Measured against a real parked
Platinum box: 2ms, versus 911ms for the same call while it was up.

The panel read `retry: true` off that body and believed it. It said "The sandbox
is starting. Files will appear automatically." — neither sentence true of a box
that only a SEND can wake — and re-issued the refused request every 3s with no
deadline. It looked like loading rather than an error because a refetch on a
query that never held data resets it to `pending` and clears the error
(query-core 5.101.2, `fetchState`), so it cycled skeleton, spinner, skeleton
until the tab closed.

Three things let that happen, and all three are fixed here.

The gate opened over a dead box. `fileServerHealthState` derived `healthy` from
the connection `status`, which nothing clears when a box parks: `use-session`
pins it to `connected` on switch with no poller, and `use-runtime-reconnect`'s
parked branch deliberately leaves it alone. The composer read the control-plane
row and said "idle" while the Files gate read the socket and said "connected".

The SDK already knew. `use-runtime-reconnect` distinguishes a PARKED box
(`hop === 'control_plane'`, answered from the row) from a BOOTING one, used the
fact to keep the stall clock off, and then dropped it. The connection store now
keeps it, so every surface can tell a wait from a dead end.

And the health probe itself was the worse loop. A parked box matches
`connected` + `healthy: false`, the same pair a booting one shows, so it
inherited POLL_FAILING: a health request every 150ms, forever, per open tab,
against a state that cannot change on its own. POLL_PARKED is 15s — still a
heartbeat, so a wake from another tab surfaces, at 4 requests a minute instead
of 400.

The panel no longer explains itself, it works: while the box is asleep the
listing comes from the project's bare git mirror at the session's own branch
(the branch name IS the session id), read-only, with write and search off.
Verified end to end — the daemon 503s in 2ms while the mirror returns the tree
in 33ms.

That fallback is guarded rather than trusted. `createRemoteSessionBranch` pushes
the branch as fire-and-forget background work that can fail, so the mirror can
come back empty; an end-to-end run caught exactly that. "Parked and empty" is
therefore the one thing the panel must not state as fact, and it says the
session is idle instead of claiming an empty folder.

Verified: 410/410 API+CLI flows, SDK 3045 pass / 0 fail, typecheck, install
smoke, route-coverage gate. Web suites show 141 pre-existing failures both with
and without this change.

* fix(session): read a parked session's files from the mirror too, and slow the re-read

Opening the Files gate over a parked box let the user click a file — and the
viewer still read bytes from the dead daemon. `use-file-content` and
`use-binary-blob` turn that `503 sandbox_not_ready` into a 3s `refetchInterval`
with no end, so the first fix would have moved the forever-spinner out of the
panel and into the preview modal. Found by walking every `isSandboxNotReadyError`
consumer rather than trusting the first one.

So the viewer follows the listing: while the box is parked,
`useFileViewerSource` returns the git-mirror-backed source, which reads the same
session branch the listing is already showing. Opening a file on an idle session
now works instead of spinning.

The re-read poll is slowed, NOT stopped. Stopping it would trade a busy wait for
a dead one: the send that wakes the box can come from the composer, another tab
or a trigger, and when it does the file has to appear without the user hunting
for a retry button. `SANDBOX_PARKED_REFETCH_INTERVAL_MS` is 30s against the 3s
boot cadence — the same reasoning as POLL_PARKED in the SDK.

* fix(web): reuse the terminal's translated asleep copy instead of new hardcoded strings

The strict i18n audit caught 6 hardcoded UI strings this branch added — the
one regression a real origin/main baseline surfaced (343 -> 344 failures). An
earlier 'baseline' run had been meaningless: `git stash` on an already-clean
tree stashes nothing, so it measured this branch twice.

Rather than mint keys and ship English into nine locale catalogs, the panels
now reuse `text3915f5ca49b3" ("The workspace went to sleep") — already
translated everywhere, and already what the Terminal panel says for exactly
this state. Two panels, one sleeping box, one sentence.

Audit: 0 hardcoded findings, 0 unresolved references, 9 locales complete.
apps/web: 9547 pass / 343 fail, an IDENTICAL failure set to origin/main.

* refactor(web): drop the readiness abstraction that nothing could reach

`explorerReadinessState` and its `asleep` branch were dead on arrival. When the

`parked` stays where it does real work: withholding write/search (both run
inside the box) and keeping "empty folder" from being asserted over a mirror
that may simply be incomplete.

Also fixes two comments this branch had made false — the viewer's re-read is
slowed to 30s, not stopped, and saying "must stop" next to code that does not

already in the code.

fix(tests): the release gate's two setup phases get independent budgets

Every API shard of the release gate has failed on `Timed out waiting for
sandbox fixture readiness` for four consecutive releases — v0.13.21, v0.13.22,
v0.13.23, v0.13.24. Nothing about the product was wrong.

`runner.ts` computed one `setupDeadline = Date.now() + 900_000` and then gave
the FIRST of two sequential waits `timeoutMs: 900_000` — the whole budget. The
second wait got `Math.max(1, setupDeadline - Date.now())`. So whenever the cold
image build legitimately used most of its 15 minutes, the runtime-readiness
wait was handed 1 millisecond and failed instantly on a session that was never
given a chance to boot.

The failed shard log is conclusive: phase one starts, no image-readiness error
is raised, the "…image and runtime ready" line never prints, and the throw is
`sandbox fixture readiness` at 942 s — 900 s of image build plus overhead, then
1 ms for the boot.

Give each phase its own ceiling: IMAGE_READY_TIMEOUT_MS 15 min,
RUNTIME_READY_TIMEOUT_MS 10 min. Against the shard's own 60-minute cap that is
25 min worst-case setup, leaving 35 min for flows that run in 19-25 min. Both
phases return immediately when the image is already baked, which is the normal
case; these ceilings only cover a cold deploy.

This is the same class as the register's "a boot budget measures lack of
progress, not wall-clock" — a budget measuring the wrong thing, reported as a
product failure.

test(ci): contain the Bun epoll_ctl flake that kills the packages lane

The @kortix/db group dies on `EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl at new
WriteStream (internal:fs/streams:244:58)` — Bun 1.3.14 on Linux leaks an epoll
registration for a dup'd stdio fd, and the reused fd number fails
EPOLL_CTL_ADD. It surfaces as "Unhandled error between tests" with an EMPTY
`1 tests failed:` list, and takes the whole lane down. Seen on 1 of 9 sampled
runs (both attempts of run 35331083850).

Upstream oven-sh/bun#37968, fixed by #38008 in Bun 1.4.2. No repo code builds
that stream, --parallel=1 cannot help (epoll_ctl EEXIST is intra-process), and
--isolate is the trigger upstream, not the cure. So: retry the db group once.

A deterministic failure fails both times and still blocks the lane, so this
absorbs a flake and never a regression. The retry warns with the original
cause so a rising rate stays visible.
