repos.description: Optimised Neural Network functions for Espressif chipsets

commits.message:
Merge branch 'perf/fc-batched-s8' into 'master'

perf(fc/s3): batched per-channel FC (weight-stationary over rows)

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!54

perf(fc/s3): batched per-channel FC, weight-stationary over rows

A sequence or attention fully-connected op has many rows (time frames)
sharing one filter. Running the per-row kernel once per row re-walks the
whole filter every time, which is weight-streaming and memory-bound.
esp_nn_fully_connected_per_ch_s8_batch processes all rows in one call: the
per-channel correction prepass runs once (it is batch-independent on the
fast path) and the loop is reordered out-channel-outer / batch-inner so
each filter row stays cache-resident across rows. Bit-identical to the
per-row kernel, which it falls back to off the fast path.

The batched entry gates on the offset-free threshold for batches > 1: the
per-row gate prices the offset-correction prepass into every row, and with
it the headline conformer FFN shape (row_len 160, input_offset 5) always
fell back to the per-row kernel.

esp_nn.h provides the public name and the ESP_NN_HAS_FC_S8_BATCH feature
flag once, after the arch header is selected: ESP32-S3 aliases its
optimised kernel, every other target falls through to the portable ANSI
one, so the API exists everywhere and consumers need a single code path
(and no target can be left without a declaration).

Measured on an ESP32-S3 conformer STT encoder (48 time frames): 3.66 s ->
2.95 s. Tests compare the batched output against the per-row reference on
the conformer shape, with input_offset 0, on a non-multiple-of-16 row
(scalar tail) and on a single row; all bit-exact on ESP32-S3.

The batch checks run as their own test_app suite (fc_per_ch_s8_batch) and
report through the pass/fail counters, so the emulated CI sees a verdict
for them; the runner's expected-suite list gains the same name.

Merge branch 'ci/testing' into 'master'

ci: run test_app on emulated targets, report profiles

See merge request espressif/esp-nn!43

fix(test_app): disable the task watchdog

One CPU-bound task that never yields: on the 96 MHz esp32h2 the suite's
longest stretch now exceeds the 5 s TWDT window, esp-emu cannot deliver
the stage-0 interrupt, and the stage-1 hardware reset restarts the suite
forever (no TEST_RESULT before the 600 s cap; 6/23 targets red). On
hardware the same watchdog only logs a warning. Hangs are still caught by
the emulator's --timeout.

ci: exercise test_app via esp-emu

Adds a test stage that runs the test_app images built by the build
matrix under esp-emu (pinned 0.41.0) and turns the app's TEST_RESULT
line into the job verdict. The build jobs stage each image as
<idf>/<target>/merged-binary.bin (tools/ci/stage_merged_bin.sh, esptool
fallback for IDF < 5.3, and only for targets the test stage can run);
tools/ci/run_emulator_tests.py runs them four at a time with --net user
and a per-run timeout, stops on panic markers (the app halts in the GDB
stub), and writes profiles.csv / summary.csv plus the logs of failed
runs to test_results/.

A run is green only when every image ran and passed: a missing
TEST_RESULT, a timeout, a panic, a reboot (a second ROM boot banner ends
the run instead of stalling to the cap), a TEST_RESULT: PASS with zero
passed cases, a suite that verified no cases, a suite from the expected
list that never ran at all (so deleting a RUN_TEST line cannot quietly
shrink the run), and a job where every image was skipped all fail it.
Skips are counted and reported.

Targets: esp-emu 0.41 models esp32c3/c5/c6/h2/p4/s31; the rest stay
build-only. esp32c5 joins the v5.5, v6.0 and master build lines and the
emulated set. esp32p4 is emulated from IDF v5.5 only: older releases
hard-code the pre-rev-v3 PIE encodings that rev v3 silicon and esp-emu
reject. esp32s31 is a master-only preview target. run_emulator_tests.py
owns that list; stage_merged_bin.sh asks it with --is-emulated rather
than duplicating it, so build jobs no longer merge and upload ten images
nothing will run.

Cycle columns are emu_ansi_cycles / emu_opt_cycles / emu_ratio with a
source column naming the emulator and its version, so nobody reads
emulator instruction counts as device performance. The job runs on
python:3.13 (not -slim: the runner's instance pre-build hook needs wget,
and the image ships curl), with an explicit 2 h timeout for 23+ runs of
up to 600 s each.

feat(test_app): pass/fail/skip counters and a machine-readable verdict

Every check in the test suites goes through TEST_PASS / TEST_FAIL /
TEST_SKIP, which print as before and tally into per-run counters. The
runner prints one line per suite and a verdict at the end:

  TEST: <suite>, passed=N, failed=N, skipped=N
  PROFILE: <suite>, ansi=<cycles>, opt=<cycles>, speedup=<x>
  TEST_SUMMARY: passed=N, failed=N, skipped=N
  TEST_RESULT: PASS|FAIL

Out-of-memory cases (a test buffer or scratch that the target cannot
allocate) are skips, not failures: the kernel was never exercised.
Genuine mismatches and scratch-guard overflows stay failures, and
TEST_RESULT is FAIL iff failed > 0.

Three ways the tally under-reported, found in review and fixed here:
the depthwise suite bailed on a getter that returns 0 (the generic-opt
targets), dropping 30 of 33 cases with a green run; fc_perf reported
its bit-exactness mismatches and allocation failures with plain printf
(passed=0 failed=0); the S3 bounded-dot check and the S3 preferred-
scratch allocations in the conv tests were uncounted. The fc_perf
dispatch-vs-assembly ratio stays advisory (noise under emulation) and is
reported separately from the verdict.

PROFILE sums every profiled section of a suite (64-bit: a reference conv
on the 96 MHz emulated esp32h2 runs hundreds of millions of cycles)
instead of echoing the last case, and RUN_TEST zeroes the counters so a
suite that profiles nothing no longer shows the previous suite's
numbers. The conv tests reset the library scratch pointer after every
case so a getter that returns 0 really runs the kernel on NULL.

The PROFILE line and the fc_perf ratio are formatted without 64-bit or
floating-point conversions, which nano-printf (the default C library for
ESP32-C2 on IDF v5.x) does not implement and would print as garbage; the
ratio verdict compares by cross-multiplication, so it is exact.

build(test_app): shared debug defaults, P4 rev v3 select, ignore lock file

Move the GDB-stub-on-panic and light heap poisoning settings from the
ESP32-P4 defaults into the shared sdkconfig.defaults so every target
halts in the stub with a backtrace instead of rebooting on a panic (on
hardware and under the emulator alike). Select the rev v3.x ESP32-P4
(CONFIG_ESP32P4_SELECTS_REV_LESS_V3=n), which is what the test boards and
esp-emu run; older IDF releases without the option ignore it. Drop the
redundant CONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED from the S31 defaults (it is in the shared
file) and ignore test_app/dependencies.lock.

commits.message:
fix: tear down WiFi when leaving the Settings network screen (#3613)

## Summary

* **What is the goal of this PR?**
* Ensure Wi-Fi resources are released when leaving `Settings → Network`,
even if the user only scans for networks.

* **What changes are included?**
* Disconnect Wi-Fi when leaving the Settings network screen and perform
a silent restart when Wi-Fi was activated.
* Add a Settings restart target so the device returns to Settings after
cleanup instead of Home.

## Additional Context

* This route did not use the normal Wi-Fi shutdown path.
`WifiSelectionActivity` is opened as a child of `SettingsActivity`; when
it closes, only the child’s `onExit()` runs. That cleanup removes scan
results but intentionally leaves Wi-Fi management to the parent. In the
other Wi-Fi flows, the parent activity exits and its `onExit()`
disconnects Wi-Fi before calling the normal silent restart. From
Settings, that parent exit never occurs, so the previous callback only
saved settings and left Wi-Fi active.
* If Wi-Fi was never enabled, no restart is requested. When it was
enabled, the cleanup restart returns the user to Settings.
* Fixes #3343

Feat/idea plugin (#1031)

* feat(idea): add IntelliJ IDEA plugin extension

Add a new JetBrains IDE extension under extensions/idea/ that brings
the Open Code Review workflow to IntelliJ-based IDEs.

The implementation mirrors the VSCode extension architecture:
- JCEF-based webview for sidebar and config panel (shared HTML/JS bundle)
- Same CLI integration (ocr review, config, install)
- Git integration via command-line git (branch/commit/workspace modes)
- Comment mounting with RangeHighlighter and inline panels
- i18n support (en/zh-cn), matching the VSCode extension
- Theme-aware CSS variables synced from IDEA's LookAndFeel

195 tests pass across 15 suites. ./gradlew runIde launches successfully.

Closes #499

* fix(idea): harden process/threading/disposal + subdir jump path-basis

Address ocr code-review findings across the host side:
- CliService: probe/runRaw/install process lifecycle (bounded joins,
  closeStreamsQuietly, SIGTERM+grace, independent install slot, atomic
  current claim), cancel getAndSet, install stale killStaleInstall.
- GitService: stdout UTF-8, reader join on timeout, getState synchronized,
  isRelevantTo case-insensitive + os.name hoist, safeRef injection guard,
  getCommitFiles dedup.
- ConfigService: atomic temp+rename write, dir 700, readRaw log, setMany
  rollback + failing-key log, @Synchronized writers, trySetPosix Windows skip.
- JCEF disposal: EDT-safe browser/dialog teardown, idempotent dispose,
  PCE rethrow, init try-catch self-cleanup, @Volatile channel.
- ReviewSession: cancel CAS, run-before-cancel guard, catch Exception+PCE.
- SidebarRouter: CancelReview target capture + identity guard, startReview
  cancels stale session.
- CommentService: jump path-basis fix (resolveProjectFile uses repoRoot to
  match repo-relative comment paths when project opened at a subdir).
- Misc: HostStrings single-pass param replace, IdeaTheme alpha clamp +
  font-name sanitization, CliParse isNotBlank, Providers Locale.ROOT,
  ConfigUtils isNotBlank + key normalization, ConfigDraft preset-key
  normalization, WebviewHtml BOM strip + IOException fallback.

* fix(idea): parsePorcelain arrow parsing for filenames containing ' -> '

When a filename contains ' -> ' (spaces + arrow), git quotes it. The old
code used indexOf(" -> ") which matched the arrow INSIDE the filename
instead of the separator, producing a corrupted path.

Fix: prioritize '" -> ' (closing quote + separator, 5 chars) which
unambiguously finds the separator for quoted paths. Fall back to ' -> '
for unquoted paths (no spaces → no false match).

Tests: 3 new cases — quoted rename, arrow-in-name rename, arrow-no-space.

* test(idea): add parsePorcelain case for unquoted-old/quoted-new rename

* chore(idea): remove unused JComponent import in OcrToolWindowFactory

* fix(idea): log JSON parse errors inside parseRawConfig

parseRawConfig's internal runCatching swallowed JSON errors silently.
readRaw's outer runCatching only catches IO errors (readText), not JSON
parse errors. Added Logger.warn inside parseRawConfig so JSON errors are
also recorded.

Note: thisLogger() unresolved from top-level function in ConfigDraft.kt
(likely inline-function context issue); used Logger.getInstance instead.

* fix(idea): path traversal guard in readWorkspaceFile + isBinaryFile

File(root, relPath) without validation allows ../../etc/passwd to
escape the repo root. Added canonicalPath.startsWith(root + separator)
check, wrapped in runCatching for graceful degradation on IO errors.

itself validates (path stays within repo tree).

* fix(idea): @Synchronized on set() to prevent race with deleteCustomProvider

set() goes through cli.runRaw (external CLI process) to write config.json,
bypassing the @Synchronized lock that deleteCustomProvider/writeRaw use.
Adding @Synchronized serializes set with deleteCustomProvider, preventing
interleaving that could silently undo config changes.

* fix(idea): @Volatile on GitService callback properties

diffDecorator and diffViewerReady are written from ReviewProjectService
(on init/dispose) and read from pooled threads (git operations). Without
@Volatile, the pooled thread may not see the latest value. Added @Volatile
for cross-thread visibility.

* fix(idea): close process streams in ShellEnv.capture via finally

Added closeStreamsQuietly() extension on Process (matching CliService
pattern) and a finally block in capture() to ensure inputStream/
outputStream/errorStream are closed on all three exit paths (timeout/
normal/interrupt). Previously only outputStream was closed (stdin at
start), inputStream fd leaked until GC.

* fix(idea): clear stale maps in show() + guard malformed FAILED + close stale streams + fix leftRefFor fallback

- CommentService: clear jumpBlockReasons/locateNotes in show() first synchronized

- GitService: leftRefFor mergeBase failure returns null instead of falling back

* fix(idea): resolveProjectFile use toRealPath to resolve symlinks

normalize() only resolves .. and . lexically, not symlinks. A symlink
inside the repo pointing outside (e.g. evil_link.txt -> /etc/passwd)
passes the startsWith check but refreshAndFindFileByNioFile resolves
to the symlink target — reading files outside the repo.

Switched normalize() to toRealPath() which resolves all symlinks,
so the startsWith check catches symlink escapes.

* fix(idea): add disposed guard to scheduleFullRepaint

Consistent with forceFullRepaint which already checks disposed.
Prevents restarting stopped timers after dispose().

* fix(idea): register OcrWebview with proper Disposer parent to fix memory leak

OcrWebview's constructor calls messageBus.connect(this), which adds
OcrWebview to the Disposer tree under ROOT_DISPOSABLE (no parent).
Neither JcefReviewPanel nor JcefConfigPanelHost registered OcrWebview
as their child, so on IDE shutdown Disposer found 11+ leaked instances.

Fix: Disposer.register(this, webview) in both JcefReviewPanel and
JcefConfigPanelHost. webview.dispose() is idempotent, so the existing
manual dispose calls in dispose() methods are safe alongside Disposer.

* fix(idea): terminate CLI process tree to prevent orphaned grandchildren

Process.destroy()/destroyForcibly() only signal the direct child. The
globally-installed ocr CLI is a Node launcher that spawns the Go binary
as a grandchild; killing only the launcher orphans the Go process, which
gets reparented to the system root and keeps running after cancellation.

Snapshot descendants before SIGTERM (handles stay valid after the parent
dies, while live enumeration goes blind due to reparenting), then
tree-kill from the snapshot after the grace period, parent first so
supervisor-like parents cannot respawn children. Applied to all six kill
sites: cancel, runRaw stale/finally, install finally, killStaleInstall,
and probe timeout. Fallback sites drop the isAlive guard to shrink the
check-then-enumerate TOCTOU window, and kill helpers never throw so
stream cleanup in finally blocks is always reached.

Adds CliServiceTreeKillTest: spawns a fake CLI with a grandchild,
cancels, and asserts the grandchild dies (POSIX only).

* build(idea): enable local Plugin Verifier and fix deprecated JCEF API

Configure pluginVerification so ./gradlew verifyPlugin has an IDE to
check against (2.x requires an explicit list); this only wires the
verification task — the packaged zip is byte-identical before/after.

Switch OcrWebview to the JBCefBrowserBase overload of JBCefJSQuery.create:
the JBCefBrowser overload is scheduled for removal and was flagged by
the verifier. Verifier verdict is now clean ("Compatible").

* ci(idea): drop gradle cache upload on self-hosted host

The idea job runs on the self-hosted host without a container, so
~/.gradle (including the ~1GB IDE distribution) already persists
between runs. setup-java's post-job cache save tried to upload a
2.4GB archive and stalled the runner, leaving the job red despite

* chore(vscode): drop accidentally committed package-lock.json

The frontend-extraction refactor ran npm install inside the vscode
extension package and committed the resulting npm lockfile. That
package is yarn-managed (yarn.lock, yarn install --frozen-lockfile

sync with yarn.lock. Nothing references it.

extensions/vscode is yarn-managed and extensions/frontend is
npm-managed; ignore the other manager's lockfile in each so an
accidental npm/yarn install cannot sneak a second lockfile into the
repo again.

fix(asciidoc): recognise a rowspan-only cell specifier (#4290)

AsciiDoc writes a cell span as [colspan][.rowspan] followed by "+" or "*", and
either number may be omitted, so ".2+" is a rowspan on its own. _CELL_SPEC
required a leading digit, matching "2+", "2.3+" and "3*" but not ".2+".

_is_table_line therefore rejected the line, and the block loop reads a
non-table line inside a table as the end of the table. One missing alternative
produced four symptoms:

  |===
  |A |B
  .2+|tall |x
  |y
  |===

gave a table truncated to its header, the ".2+" row dropped, "|y" emitted as a
literal text item, and a spurious 0x0 table at the end, because in_table had
already been reset when the closing "|===" was read and it opened a new one.

The pattern now accepts a span whose colspan is absent, while still requiring
at least one of the two numbers so a bare "+" does not match. Measured over
"2+", ".2+", "2.2+", "3*", ".3*", "^", ".^", "h", "a" and "^.^h": only the two
rowspan-only forms change, and "+" and "*" alone still do not match.

Out of scope, and pre-existing: a row with fewer cells than the header still
leaves a spurious 0x0 table. That reproduces without this change, from both
"|3" on its own and "2+|wide", so it is a different defect. The backend also
strips every specifier and hardcodes row_span and col_span to 1, so a
recognised span is not yet honoured; that needs grid placement and is a larger
change.

Tests: uv run pytest tests/test_backend_asciidoc.py

Signed-off-by: chrikrah <48338417+chrikrah@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(html): default a zero colspan or rowspan to 1 in HTML tables (#4287) _get_cell_spans accepts a span attribute when its first character is numeric, so "0" passes the guard and reaches the table grid as a span of 0. The cell then covers no grid position at all: its text is dropped from the table and the cells after it shift into the place it should have taken. For AB the grid came out as [["B"]] with num_cols 1, instead of [["A", "B"]] with num_cols 2. The docstring already promises a default of 1 when the attribute is absent or not numeric, and the same guard already catches a negative value such as "-3". Zero was the one value that slipped through. Clamping to 1 is a deliberate minimum rather than full conformance. HTML5 requires colspan to be greater than zero, but it gives rowspan its own zero case: the value zero means that the cell is to span all the remaining rows in the row group. This change does not implement that rule. It keeps the cell in the output instead of losing it, and the row-group semantics can follow separately. Signed-off-by: chrikrah <48338417+chrikrah@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
perf: avoid the intermediate array in from_entries (#3626)

Define `from_entries` as `add(.[] | f) // {}` instead of
`map(f) | add // {}`. Since `add(f)` is `reduce f as $x (null; . + $x)`,
both fold the same values in the same order from the same seed, so the
only difference is that the array of single-key objects built by `map`
is never materialized.

Measured with both the generator and the result suppressed, so that only
the `from_entries` work differs: 6-15% less user time across input shapes,
which is 10-24% of what `from_entries` itself costs. For inputs above
roughly a thousand entries, peak RSS drops by 37%, around 80% of the
memory `from_entries` adds on top of its input; a 1,000,000 entry array
goes from 1064 MiB to 672 MiB.

Register imported libraries in dependency order (#3620)

block_mark_referenced walks the joined block backwards and skips the
body of any definition not yet marked referenced, so a library must
precede its importers.  f58787c41 registered a library before walking
its dependencies, to have somewhere to keep the `loading` flag, which
reversed that order and made block_drop_unreferenced free definitions
that are still referenced through bound_by.

Keep the libraries being loaded on a stack threaded through the
load_library frames instead, so registration can move back after the
dependency walk.
Implement `range/3` in C for consistent error handling (#3267)

Use WriteConsoleW() in priv_fwrite() too (#3607)

jq dumps JSON to the Windows console as UTF-16 with WriteConsoleW(),
but priv_fwrite() still writes the raw UTF-8 bytes with WriteFile(),
which the console decodes with its output code page.  So `jq .k` prints
non-ASCII correctly while `jq -r .k` prints mojibake, and the same goes
for -j, --raw-output0, --seq, halt_error and the `stderr` builtin.

The tty flag is computed once, from stdout, and passed to writes aimed
at stderr too, so ask the handle instead: with stdout on a console and
stderr redirected, WriteConsoleW() failed on the file handle and the
output was dropped.

One byte-level change: with stdout on a console and stderr redirected,
halt_error and the `stderr` builtin now go through the CRT, so bare LF
becomes CRLF and an existing CRLF becomes CR CRLF.  Use -b for
byte-exact output on that stream.

docs: clarify ownership of jv arguments and results (#3627)

The ownership comment in `jv.h` currently says every `jv_*` function
except `jv_copy` consumes its input. Several accessors and
object-iteration functions borrow their arguments instead, which makes
that guidance misleading for callers and language bindings.

Document the borrowing exceptions beside their declarations, including

The whole seconds were truncated toward zero while the fractional part
was measured from the floor, so any negative non-integral timestamp was
rendered one second late; gmtime was not monotonic across the epoch.

signature, and source tarball lists; older versions move into
collapsible `<details>` sections. Condense the repetitive per-version
checksum and signature sentences into a single list.

[vllm] fix: prevent scheduler resume race during async weight sync (#7846)

### What does this PR do?

Fully async weight synchronization can deadlock when a duplicate
scheduler resume overlaps with the start of a new DP request wave.

Restoring the KV cache implicitly resumes vllm scheduling, and the
subsequent resume_generation() call resumes it again. In the current
vLLM version, resume_scheduler() branches on the rank-local
[`engines_running`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dbf49dad11e30ec5d464be74b715a9a9e31c2c5a/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2110)
flag. A new request wave can cause some ranks to skip the resume
collective while others enter it, leaving EngineCores and model workers
waiting on each other until Gloo times out.

Split replica resume into two ordered phases:
- Keep request admission closed while the head server resumes all DP
EngineCores and waits for the resume RPC to complete.
- Open submission gates on all servers only after engine resume returns.

This prevents waiting generation tasks from starting a new DP wave while
the duplicate resume is still in progress. Also order the server-level
resume_generation() wrapper to resume engines before opening its gate.

Keep the explicit resume because it is still required when KV-cache
restoration is skipped.

<details>
    <summary>See here for detailed walkthrough about the race</summary>

There is a race that triggers a deadlock during weight synchronization
in fully async mode. Some ranks are blocked inside
`DPEngineCoreProc.resume_scheduler()`, while some ranks are waiting
inside model execution until they both timeout. The root cause is the
race between **duplicate scheduler resume and the start of a new DP
request wave**.

During each weight update, verl calls the same vLLM
`DPEngineCoreProc.resume_scheduler()` method twice:

1. **Implicitly**, when
[`wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/9e0252efba42a5442bbe52f7d0d2ac68e514581e/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py#L892)
restores the remaining memory and resumes scheduling.
2. **Explicitly**, through the subsequent
[`resume_generation()`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/9e0252efba42a5442bbe52f7d0d2ac68e514581e/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/vllm_async_server.py#L995)
call.

The affected vLLM implementation is not idempotent: a duplicate resume
can enter a collective even though scheduling is already unpaused. It
branches on the rank-local
[`engines_running`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/dbf49dad11e30ec5d464be74b715a9a9e31c2c5a/vllm/v1/engine/core.py#L2110)
flag. Since request-wave notifications and resume RPCs arrive
independently, one rank can see `True` and return immediately, while
another sees `False` and enters the resume barrier. That creates a
circular wait:

- B’s EngineCore waits for A’s EngineCore to join the resume collective.
- A’s workers wait for B’s workers to join the model collective.
- B’s EngineCore cannot dispatch work to its workers while blocked in
the resume collective.

This deadlock eventually reported as Gloo timeouts.
</details>

[vLLM PR #55229](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55229),
currently a draft, addresses this vllm issue by recognizing duplicate
resumes using scheduler pause state and the wave gate. Already-unpaused
ranks skip synchronization consistently, while genuine resumes retain
the barrier.

commits.message:
fix(apps): stop the db/file commands from misdirecting the caller on failure (#2719)

* fix(apps): classify the db publish-approval rejection instead of hinting at multi-env

When an app's release goes through publish approval, the server refuses
+db-env-migrate with subcode k_dl_4000052. That subcode was unmapped, so the
failure surfaced as subtype "unknown" carrying the per-command fallback hint
("ensure the app is multi-env and has pending dev changes"), which points at two
things that are both already correct and sends the caller to +db-env-create — an
irreversible no-op here. No flag, environment or app id makes the CLI path
succeed while the approval is configured, so the failure has to read as "not via
this channel" rather than "fix the request".

- Map k_dl_4000052 in dbSubcodeTable as api/feature_not_available; the hint
  states that the app requires release approval, names the two ways to release
  it (+release-create or the web console), and notes that +db-env-diff still
  previews the pending changes
- Keep exit 1: exit 2 would tell an agent to change the request and retry, exit 3
  would send it to re-authenticate, and neither can succeed
- Document the rejection under +db-env-migrate in the apps db reference so agents
  move to the release flow instead of retrying

* fix(apps): point the file commands' --jq examples at the envelope

--jq runs against the whole response envelope, but three file commands
advertised bare payload paths: +file-quota-get suggested -q '.usage_percent',
+file-get suggested -q '.size_bytes' / -q '.download_url', and +file-upload
suggested -q '.path'. Every one of them resolves to null and still exits 0 —
the worst shape for an agent, which reads a successful exit with an empty value
as "the server returned nothing" rather than "the example is wrong". The other
eight --jq examples in this domain already carry the .data prefix, so these
three were the outliers.

- Prefix the four expressions with .data, matching the rest of the domain
- Note on +file-quota-get that usage_percent only appears once a quota is
  provisioned; the command omits it (with storage_quota_bytes) when the backend
  reports quota 0, so the example would otherwise look broken against an app
  that has no quota yet
- Add TestTips_JQExpressionsAddressTheEnvelope, which rejects any tip whose --jq
  path starts outside the envelope's top-level keys. The check is structural, so
  it needs no live response and covers commands whose payload shape is
  server-dependent
- Split the root extraction into jqRootField and cover it directly: expressions
  that name no field (".", ".?", ". | .", ".[]") are all valid jq, and indexing
  the split result would have panicked on two of them and misread ".[]" as the
  field "]"

* fix(apps): report usage_percent at one decimal in both quota commands

+db-quota-get and +file-quota-get passed the server's raw percentage straight
through, so a 2 GB quota produced readings like 5.40924072265625 and
0.4398345947265625. The tail is float64 representation noise, not measurement —
it resolves to roughly a megabyte on that quota, while the companion
storage_used_bytes already carries the exact figure. It reads as false precision
and costs an agent context on digits that carry nothing.

- Round usage_percent to one decimal in both projections via a shared
  roundUsagePercent, so the two commands cannot drift apart
- Keep it a JSON number rather than a formatted string: callers compare it
  (-q '.data.usage_percent > 80'), and whole values encode as "2" not "2.0"
- Do not clamp above 100 — the server deliberately reports over-quota as-is, and
  folding 180% to 100% would hide the one reading that must stay visible
- Leave the field out entirely when it is absent or non-numeric, rather than
  writing a 0 that would read as "nothing used"
- Cover the wire-observed values, the whole-number and over-quota cases, and a
  json.Marshal assertion so a rounded float cannot serialise a tail back

pretty output is unchanged: it already formatted with %.1f.

* test(apps): cover the download_url round trip in the file commands

A download_url the platform hands out was rejected by the very commands that
take a --path: +file-get, +file-sign and +file-download all answered 400000034
"File not found or no access". An agent cannot tell that apart from a genuinely
missing file, so it reads the platform's own output as invalid and stops. The
resolution is server-side — the CLI forwards --path verbatim — so a unit test
cannot see a regression here and only a live call can.

- Upload a file, read its download_url back rather than constructing one (a
  hand-built URL would test this test's idea of the format, not the format
  callers are actually handed), then feed it to all three commands
- Assert each resolves to the real path, and compare the downloaded bytes: a
  response that wrote an error body would still exit 0
- Add a negative case so the compatibility cannot degrade into "accept
  anything" — an absent file must still fail not_found in both the plain-path
  and download_url shapes, which is also what stops the positive cases from
  passing against a server that skipped the lookup entirely
- Fixture-gated like the sibling upload workflow, and deletes what it uploads

Verified to discriminate: green against a backend carrying the fix, and red on
exactly the three round-trip cases (negative case still green) against one
without it.

* fix(apps): stop reporting a wrong app id as a missing permission

The storage permission chain answered three unrelated states with one code and
one sentence — "user need admin or developer permission": the caller genuinely
lacked a role, the app could not be found, or the argument was never an app id
at all. Only the first is a permission problem. The other two sent people off to
request access they already had, and sent agents to exit 3, which says
"re-authenticate" and cannot resolve either.

The backend now separates them. This is the client half.

- Reject a non-app_ --app-id in the file commands' Validate via requireFileAppID,
  so a meta token or a page token fails locally with exit 2 and a hint carrying
  the +get invocation that converts it into an app_id. The prefix rule stays out
  of requireAppID: +export and +get accept an app id or a meta token in the same
  argument, so a blanket check would break them
- Classify the two new backend codes: 400000008 (app not found) as api/not_found,
  matching the neighbouring file-not-found arm, and 400000009 (malformed app id)
  as validation/invalid_argument. Neither may stay under authorization
- Cover the gate per command rather than only through the helper: a helper wired
  into some of the seven commands would pass a helper-level test and still ship
  the defect
- Add e2e for both halves. The malformed case is a dry-run — the rejection
  happens before a request is built — while app-not-found can only be judged
  live, and asserts negatively (must not be authorization / exit 3) so a
  regression cannot hide behind a renamed code

* test(apps): pin that a real permission failure stays a permission failure

Splitting "app not found" out of the shared permission error is only half a
contract. The other half is that the state which genuinely is a permission
problem keeps reporting as one: an over-correction that swept it into not_found
would tell a caller the app does not exist when it does, and would hide the fact
that access can actually be requested.

- Add TestAppsFileNoPermissionLive on its own fixture, since it needs something
  the other cases do not — an app that exists in the tenant and that the caller
  has no role on
- Assert both directions: authorization / permission_denied, and explicitly not
  not_found, so the two cases cannot converge again

Verified to discriminate: against a backend carrying the split, the not-found
case passes and this one passes; against one without it, the not-found case
fails while this one still passes, which is exactly the asymmetry that tells the
two states apart.

* test(apps): configure the app-id dry-run case instead of inheriting a config

The case asserted the --app-id gate but never set up a config dir, so on a
machine that has never been configured the run stopped at the config gate and
the envelope under assertion was "not configured" rather than the validation
error. It passed locally only because an ambient config happened to exist, and
failed in CI — which is exactly the environment the case is meant to represent.

- Call setAppsDryRunEnv, the convention the other dry-run cases already use, so
  the run reaches Validate on a clean machine
- Read the envelope stdout-first then stderr, matching validateErrorMessage:
  domains differ on which stream carries it, and pinning one couples the
  assertions to runner-internal routing rather than to the contract

Verified by re-running with an empty environment and a throwaway HOME, which is
what the CI failure was.

* fix(apps): drop the classification for a code storage no longer returns

Storage briefly answered a malformed app id with its own code, and this branch
mapped it. It now reports that shape as "app not found" like any other id that
does not resolve, so the separate mapping classifies something that never
arrives.

- Remove the entry and its test row. Keeping a classification for an unobserved
  code is the mirror of guessing one: it reads as a handled case, and the next
  person has no way to tell it apart from a live mapping
- Correct the two comments that claimed storage names this shape. It does not,
  and that is precisely why requireFileAppID matters — "app not found" is true
  but points at verifying an id the caller never had, while the local check names
  the argument and carries the command that converts the token into an app id

Re-verified against the current backend: no role stays authorization / exit 3,
an absent app is not_found / exit 1, and a non-app_ argument is rejected locally
as validation / exit 2 before a request is built.

fix(drive): accept successful folder moves without a task ID (#2751)

Treat a successful folder move without a nonempty task ID as synchronous
completion, returning status=success and ready=true. Continue polling
returned task IDs, including "0", and preserve typed API failures.

Add focused regression tests and clarify conditional task polling in
dry-run output and command guidance.

perf(moe): read missing experts in parallel with pread before the slot writes (#3589)

Every expert cache miss was a synchronous memmap copy on the compute
thread, one projection tensor at a time. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (48 layers
x 512 experts, ~1.84 MB per expert) a 3461-token prompt spent 30 s in TTFT
at 68.8% residency and 183 s at 25%: almost all of it waiting on serial
reads that have no dependency on each other.

CheckpointExpertStore now opens one read-only descriptor per shard up
front and splits a fetch into a plan, a pure-bytes read (os.pread, so it
carries its own offset and needs no lock) and the host-side conversion.
ExpertCache.ensure classifies a call's misses without touching any cache
state, starts their reads on a shared pool, and then runs the same serial
install loop as before, taking bytes from the pipeline instead of reading
them itself.

Invariants preserved: slot_of insertion order, eviction victims, the
hit/miss counters, the per-slot assignment order and the bf16 uint16
transport are all unchanged, and every mutation still happens on the
calling thread in the serial order - the pool only changes when the bytes
arrive. An expert unseated by eviction between the two passes falls back
to a serial read. OMLX_MOE_OFFLOAD_IO_WORKERS=1 (or anything unparseable)
keeps the old path and starts no threads; OMLX_MOE_OFFLOAD_IO_BATCH bounds
the experts in flight, and with them the host memory the pipeline holds
ahead of the writes. Concurrent ensure() on one cache stays unsupported.

Co-authored-by: jundot <jundot@users.noreply.github.com>
refactor(cache): simplify pooling boundary integration (#3290)

Fix/glm5 promoted boundary (depends on PR #3290) (#3710)

* fix(cache): blank sliceable CacheList members in boundary snapshots when pm-plan is None

For hybrid CacheList layers where cachelist_pm_member_plan returns None
(e.g. GLM-5.x CacheList(KVCache, PoolingCache) — PoolingCache is absent
from _PM_SAFE_NON_SLICEABLE_SUBS), _extract_snapshot_cache_states left
the sliceable KVCache member un-blanked, so every in-memory boundary
snapshot retained the sparse layers' full KV prefix. That made snapshot
retention quadratic across a request — measured ~113GB phys and a guard
abort at ~30K tokens on GLM-5.3-Flash.

Blank any member whose class is a known-sliceable type even when the
per-member plan is None. To keep the persisted blocks restorable (the
legacy store path reads the KV member from the boundary snapshot),
_cachelist_snapshot_sub_tensors now refills blanked members from the
live cache's corresponding member, sliced to the block's token range.
Non-sliceable members (PoolingCache/ArraysCache) stay authoritative.

Covered by test_glm_pooling_cachelist_blanks_kv_member and
test_glm_pooling_cachelist_blanked_kv_roundtrips.

* fix(cache): persist and rebuild PoolingCache delta chains in pm boundary blocks

Address maintainer review #3290 (jundot, 2026-08-31):

- store: a compacted PoolingCache boundary member on the per-member path
  now persists as PoolingCacheDelta with its absolute pooled row range
  (the delta range was previously dropped, leaving an unlabeled per-block
  delta on disk)
- restore: the per-member branch rebuilds the PoolingCache delta chain in
  block order instead of last-blocking (which restored one block's pooled
  rows instead of the cumulative chain); chain rebuild is shared with the
  legacy cumulative path via one helper
- align cachelist_pm_class_eligible with cachelist_pm_member_plan:
  BatchPoolingCache is NOT boundary-eligible (compact_pooling_cache_snapshot
  only compacts PoolingCache), so its layers keep the legacy path and the
  signature expectation no longer stamps a pm layout stores cannot produce
- tests: round-trip now goes through Scheduler._extract_snapshot_cache_states
  + compact_pooling_cache_snapshot (the maintainer's repro), asserting
  PoolingCacheDelta markers on persisted blocks and full pooled-chain
  restore in block order; flip the pooling-member classification case and
  pin BatchPoolingCache plan/class-eligibility agreement

Rebased onto main (includes #3332 MLX 0.32.2 and the boundary-snapshot
validation fix).

* fix(cache): align boundary eligibility and drop unsafe non-pm snapshot blanking

Found while verifying #3290 integration end to end:

- the scheduler's non-pm fallback blanked known-sliceable members of
  plan-ineligible CacheList layers, but the legacy store refills those
  members with PER-BLOCK slices while the legacy restore takes the LAST
  block's state — CacheList(KVCache, BatchPoolingCache) restored KV
  truncated to one block (silent corruption). The fallback branch is
  removed: non-pm layers keep cumulative snapshots (legacy semantics);
  the linear-retention win comes only from pm eligibility, where store
  and restore agree on slicing.
- BatchPoolingCache joins _PM_SAFE_NON_SLICEABLE_SUBS (matching
  _PM_BOUNDARY_SUB_CLASSES): its boundary state (buf_kv, buf_gate,
  pooled) is self-contained at the boundary and it is not compacted, so
  it persists as a plain cumulative boundary member and restores
  last-block-wins — safe on the pm path, and batched serving actually
  produces BatchPoolingCache (deepseek_v4 _make_cache conversion).
- tests: KVCache+BatchPoolingCache pm round-trip (full KV + boundary
  state, plain marker on disk); pooled-chain edge cases — partial match
  rebuilds a truncated chain in block order, a gapped chain is rejected,
  uncompacted snapshots persist plain, and plain+deltas mixed chains are
  contiguous-safe in both orders.

* test(cache): reproduce pooled history loss in promoted GLM boundary

Exercise scheduler boundary promotion and both KV refill paths. On PR 3290 at 82e66bb2, the three-block cases restore one pooled row instead of three; one-block controls pass.

* fix(cache): preserve delta ranges from promoted boundary store sources

The scheduler removes the last snapshot from intermediate_snapshots and promotes it to cache_data. Read pooling_delta_ranges from whichever layer supplies the boundary state. Otherwise the final pooled delta is stamped as a full PoolingCache and reconstruction resets all preceding pooled rows.

commits.message:
fix: qrandint/qlograndint never sample the documented inclusive upper bound (#1606)

* fix: qrandint/qlograndint never sample the documented inclusive upper bound

Quantized.sample()'s q=1 fast path skips quantization and calls the wrapped
Integer sampler directly, which draws exclusive of domain.upper, same as
plain randint. Since qrandint defaults to q=1, its own "upper is also
inclusive (!)" docstring was never true. For q>1 the general branch rounds
a raw exclusive-upper draw, so reaching the nominal upper depends on the
rounding fraction.

Fixed by extending the sampled range by one quantization step for Integer
domains before drawing, then clamping back to the true upper bound. Plain
randint/lograndint never go through Quantized, so they are untouched.

Fixes #1605

* fix: sample quantization grid indices directly, not rounded draws

The q=1 fast path for Integer domains routed through float division,
turning integer samples into np.float64 and losing precision above
2**53. For q>1, extending the raw draw's range by a full q and
clamping the overshoot into the top bin gave that bin roughly 1.4x
the width of an interior bin (measured with a fixed seed: 40164 vs
~39800 draws per bin over 200000 samples on a 5-bin grid, expected
40000 each).

Draw the grid point's index directly instead: every point, including
the top one, is reachable through exactly one raw index, so no bin
is over- or under-represented and the result stays a plain int with
no rounding.

Added scalar/batched dtype tests, a large-bound precision test past
2**53, and a fixed-seed bin distribution test that would have caught
the top-bin bias.

* fix: sample real grid indices, not ones rebased to 1, and use exact integer arithmetic

Addresses thinkall's second review round on #1606: qlograndint drew log-
uniformly over an index range rebased to start at 1, which is a different,
shifted distribution from the actual value grid whenever lower > q (log-
uniform is scale-invariant under multiplication, not under an additive
shift). Switched to the grid's own index (value // q). Also replaced the
remaining float division for computing grid bounds with integer ceiling/
floor division, and the batched Integer path now returns an int64 ndarray
instead of a Python list, matching the historical container and dtype.

* fix: preserve list return for batched q>1 quantized integer sampling

Quantized.sample()'s Integer branch unconditionally returned an ndarray
for size > 1, but only q == 1 historically did; q > 1 returned a plain
Python list (matching the float quantization path's list(quantized)).
Return a list for q > 1 and keep the ndarray only for q == 1.

Updated the two tests that asserted ndarray for a q > 1 domain so they
check the correct historical container instead.

* fix: preserve batched q=1 sampler dtype in Quantized.sample

* fix: avoid int64 overflow multiplying quantized batch indices by q

Grid points above 2**63 - 1 wrapped silently through numpy int64
multiplication in the batched q > 1 Integer path; multiply each index
as a Python int instead.

* fix: restore CRLF line endings in flaml/tune/sample.py

The prior merge from main flattened this file's CRLF line endings to
LF, so the PR diff showed the whole file as removed and re-added
instead of the actual ~30-line change.

* fix: restrict Quantized's integer grid-index transform to the two built-in samplers

A custom sampler on an Integer domain got the grid-index domain (and,
for q > 1, its output multiplied by q) unconditionally, which breaks
any sampler that reads domain.lower/domain.upper or returns actual
values rather than an index. Only Integer._Uniform and
Integer._LogUniform use the grid transform now; every other sampler
keeps the historical actual-value contract, q == 1 calling it directly
and q > 1 falling through to the existing float-based quantization.

* fix: restore float unit quantization at q == 1

The custom-sampler-contract fix (6320d970) widened the q == 1 direct
passthrough from Integer-only to isinstance(domain, Integer) == False
domains too, so a Float domain (quniform/qloguniform/qrandn) at q == 1
skipped the round-to-nearest-unit step entirely and returned the raw
unrounded sample. Scope the passthrough back to Integer domains, which
is what it was gating before this round's change.

test/tune/test_unit_quantization.py::test_unit_quantization_rounds_float_samples
covers this; it fails on the current head (6 of 18 parametrizations,
all q=1) and passes with this fix.

commits.message:
change: openraft: gate heartbeats after quorum loss

# Summary

Add an opt-in heartbeat gate that alternates quiet and send periods after a
Leader's quorum evidence expires, giving the reachable quorum time to elect a
replacement.

# Details

`Config::quorum_loss_probe_interval` sets each phase length. The phase is
derived from the latest quorum-acknowledged timestamp, or
`RaftState::vote_last_modified()` before the first quorum acknowledgement, so
the policy needs no activity state, commands, or coordination channel.

Only heartbeat emission is gated. Replication and snapshots continue, and a
fresh quorum acknowledgement immediately restores normal heartbeat behavior.
`None` preserves existing behavior. The interval must be at least
`leader_lease + election_timeout_max`.

Upgrade tip: Add `quorum_loss_probe_interval` to exhaustive `Config` literals
and handle `ConfigError::QuorumLossProbeIntervalTooSmall` in exhaustive
matches. Existing named-field configurations default the new field to `None`.

- Fix: #2080

fix: Use default value for initial RaftMetrics

Previously, when creating a new `RaftMetrics` object via
`RaftMetrics::new_initial` the `state` field was set to
`ServerState::Follower` instead of the default value
`ServerState::Learner`. This was confusing for a couple of reasons.

It disagreed with the initial value set in
`RaftServerMetrics::new_initial`, which is the default value of
`ServerState::Learner`.

It disagreed with the logic in `RaftState::calc_server_state`, which
returns `ServerState::Learner` for nodes that are not in the membership
state. When a `RaftMetrics` is first created, and there's no membership
data, `ServerState::Follower` is returned.

A Default variant implies that this is the variant that should be used
when no other information is known. So it was strange that we weren't
using the Default variant in this scenario.

test: membership: wait for commit tracking reset

# Summary

Make the uncommitted-leader-log test wait for the new leader's commit
tracking to reset before checking the diagnostic error.

# Details

Leadership metrics can briefly retain the prior term's cluster-committed
log after the new leader starts receiving quorum acknowledgements. Waiting
for the reset removes the scheduling race exposed by the initial
RaftMetrics state change.

commits.message:
ota: bounds check on /api/flash only covers the first chunk, and runs after init_ota (#2189)

* ota: check the whole upload against maxaddr, and check it before init_ota

Two things went wrong here, both reachable from one POST to /api/flash/<addr>.

The bounds check tested writelen, which is only the part of the body that
arrived with the headers, usually well under a kilobyte. The loop underneath
then writes towrite bytes, which comes from Content-Length, advancing startaddr
as it goes and never checking again. A large Content-Length with a small first
chunk therefore walks straight past maxaddr. Check towrite, since that is what
actually gets written.

The check also ran after init_ota, which clears flash write protection and
mallocs the sector buffer. Bailing out at that point returns without
close_ota(), so the buffer is never freed and protection is never restored.
init_ota refuses to start while sector is non-null, so one rejected upload
leaves OTA broken until the next reboot. Validate first, then init.

* ota: make the range check overflow safe and reject empty writes

startaddr + towrite is signed arithmetic, so a large content length can
wrap it negative and the sum then compares below maxaddr, passing the
check it was meant to fail. Compare with a subtraction instead, with the
operands guarded first so maxaddr - startaddr cannot go negative, and
reject a zero length in the same condition so an empty post no longer
reaches init_ota.

Enable ping watchdog (compiled out since 1.18.16) (#2229)

* Enable ping watchdog

- new_ping.c was compiled out since eb5b1ca2 added the guards: the macro was
  referenced in five files and defined in none
- the counter was armed and incremented outside the guard while its only
  reset lived inside it, so devices reported a runaway secondsWithNoPing
  while transmitting nothing
- last good release 1.18.15, first affected 1.18.16

* Remove unused lwip/prot/ip4.h include from new_ping.c

HA discovery: fix use-after-free / double free of dev_info (#2230) (#2234)

The toggle/dimmer pairing block frees dev_info but does not clear it:

    dev_info = hass_init_light_singleColor_onChannels(toggle, dimmer, brightness_scale);
    MQTT_QueuePublish(topic, dev_info->channel, hass_build_discovery_json(dev_info), OBK_PUBLISH_FLAG_RETAIN);
    hass_free_device_info(dev_info);
    discoveryQueued = true;          /* dev_info still points at freed memory */

The LED block a few lines later guards on exactly that pointer:

    if (dev_info == NULL) {
        dev_info = hass_init_light_device_info(LIGHT_RGBCW);
    }
    MQTT_QueuePublish(topic, dev_info->channel, hass_build_discovery_json(dev_info), ...);
    hass_free_device_info(dev_info);

hass_free_device_info() takes the pointer by value, so it cannot null the
caller's variable. The guard therefore does not fire, and the block reads
->channel and serialises ->root from freed memory, then frees it a second time.

On a TuyaMCU LED device - the only configuration that runs both blocks - this
publishes a second discovery message for the same topic. Observed on a BK7231T:

    Queued topic=homeassistant/light/OpenBK7231T_0668EFA8_light_1/config, 1 items in queue
    Queued topic=homeassistant/light/OpenBK7231T_0668EFA8_light_1/config, 2 items in queue
    Publishing val (374 bytes) to homeassistant/light/OpenBK7231T_0668EFA8_light_1/config retain=1
    Publishing val {} to homeassistant/light/OpenBK7231T_0668EFA8_light_1/config retain=1

The "{}" is the already-deleted cJSON. Publishing it retained to a discovery
topic also removes the entity from Home Assistant.

When the freed block has already been reused the topic itself is garbage. With
the web UI open it came back as a fragment of the page's HTML, and the broker
dropped the connection as a malformed packet.

Fix: clear the pointer after freeing, matching the two other free sites in this
function which already do.

driver: add an RTC driver for BK7252N (#2208)

* driver: add an RTC driver for BK7252N

The BK7252N has an always-on RTC counter that the SDK already uses as the
time base for rtos_get_time_us(), but nothing exposes it to the
application. This driver anchors that counter to NTP once and then
advances the wall clock in hardware, so the time stays correct while NTP
is unreachable instead of being carried by the software second counter.

The index page and the new RTCTime command also report how far the
software counter has drifted from the hardware one.

Enabled by ENABLE_DRIVER_RTC, set for BK7252N only.

* driver: rename the RTC driver symbols to BKRTC

RTC_Init clashed with a declaration of the same name in the Realtek SDK,
which broke the RTL8710B, RTL8720D, RTL8720E and RTL8721DA builds: the
prototypes in drv_local.h are compiled on every platform, while the
driver body is not. The BKRTC prefix matches the neighbouring BKCharge
driver and leaves no ambiguity about which RTC is meant.

* bkrtc: anchor again only on a fresh NTP response and keep the epoch in UTC

NTP_IsTimeSynced() stays true once the first response has arrived, and
NTP_GetCurrentTime() returns the software device clock rather than a fresh
sample. Comparing the epoch derived from the RTC against that clock every
second and rebasing on a five second disagreement therefore tied the RTC
clock back to the software clock it was meant to be independent of: once
NTP went away, any drift of the software clock would be copied into the
RTC base.

Count genuine NTP responses in the NTP driver and let the RTC driver rebase
only when that count has moved, so a stale sync can never anchor it again.
The drift against the software clock is still measured every second, since
that number is what the driver exists to report. Anchor from the UTC device
time so the epoch carries no timezone or DST offset, do the drift
subtraction in signed 64 bit arithmetic instead of relying on the unsigned
wraparound, and drop the time base if the hardware counter ever reads lower
than the base, so the elapsed subtraction cannot underflow. The driver
description no longer claims the clock stays correct while NTP is
unreachable.

The converter was launched with stderr=null, so any failure message

  2. lsm import --lsm-database ... --lsm-import-from ... --snapshot ...

Sync the ty security mirror (#4549)

`ty-security` needs to follow public `main` while its default branch
remains locked. Add an STS-backed workflow and a policy rule granting it
`contents: write` and `workflows: write` only for the pinned
`ty-security` repository ID. The sync fast-forwards to a verified public
commit, refuses private or divergent history, and keeps private objects
and remote diagnostics out of the public workflow. After this lands,
`ty-security/main` needs a one-time fast-forward to receive the policy
before automated sync can authorize itself.

checks out the current repository, preventing authenticated checkout in
a private copy. Grant `contents: read` to the reusable workflow and its
release caller, and record the caller permission in
`dist-workspace.toml` so regeneration retains it.

commits.message: ci: support Xcode 27 builds

Adopt the iOS 15 minimum deployment target across the codebase

Follow-up to #689, which raised the deployment target to iOS 15.0 in the
Xcode project, Package.swift, and the podspec.

- Bump swift-tools-version to 5.5 and update the README, CHANGELOG, and
  the SwiftUI API guide for the new requirement
- Remove @available / #available branches for iOS 14 and earlier from the
  library, tests, and examples
- Make statePublisher non-optional and cornerCurve a stored property
- Replace the deprecated VisualEffectBlur in Maps-SwiftUI with Material
- Drop UnavailableViewController from Samples and fix deprecation warnings
  surfaced by the new target
- Raise the example apps' deployment targets to iOS 15.0
- Drop the Xcode 15.4 / iOS 17 jobs from CI
